I rarely review games. The only other review I have written was of "The Last of Us." This game was also a very well crafted narrative with engrossing characters and environments. The fact that your choices matter draws you even deeper into the story. I would wager that I, as a man in my 30s, am farther from the drama of high school girls than anyone out there. Yet, I was caught up in the story and the relationships. I felt for the characters and wanted to do what I could to ensure the best outcomes for them.
Some have argued that the time travel power makes your decisions feel less impactful, but I find that I found the presence of the power made me more conscious of the choices I was making. After all, it is a game, and in other decision-based games, you make the best choice based on the one or two word descriptor or save the character you like better, and what happens happens. You might go back and play again and make different choices, but then it's hard to remember the choices you made before. This game is compared to other games, like Telltale's Walking Dead, and I see the similarity. However, here the game makes the decision making process part of the story and part of the main character's evolution. I, as the player, felt very much like Max must have. You have the power to change things, so you want to make sure you've made the best possible choice. You still can't really know until much later. It also let's you experiment with different approaches, experience more of the excellent voice acting, explore the characters and their motivations in depth, and get some schadenfreude out of your system to boot! Win win!
*Spoilers ahead*
Ultimately, the game is a fable about unintended consequences. The references to "climate change," which is the unintended consequence of our industrial societies and lifestyles, echo that theme. From the first scene, the game  foreshadows that things are not right in the "space-time contnuum," and it is implied throughout that Max's temporal exploits are having unforeseen repercussions. So the ending, which many found disappointing, fits with that overall theme. I found the ending acceptable, although not perfect. I understand the criticisms of an ending which seems to negate the player's efforts to that point, but I would argue that even if you choose to "undo" what you've done, the nefarious criminals are still brought to justice through the exploits of Max and Chloe throughout the week. Even if, in the end, the week did not "happen," except for Max, it still had meaning for her, and will impact her life and relationships for the rest of her life. She gained confidence and perspective. She came out of her shell, which is also one of the themes driven home repeatedly. It is her story, after all. The final choice is the culmination of her coming of age story about unintended consequences. It cements the point that no matter how much we try to plan and make good choices, ultimately, life is...well...strange.
I would recommend this game for the story, characters, music, and novelty. I have often wished I could turn back time for a few moments to make a better choice, and in this game you can live that.

Imagine the most intricate, accurate to life space vehicle simulator you can.  Dozens of toggle switches, displays ranging from the strange and esoteric to the vague and incomprehensible, buttons flashing angrily at you and daring you to press them.  The screen shakes and aside from the roar of liftoff, the only thing you can hear is your own labored breathing and the pulse in your ears.  Do you have this picture in your head?  Good.
Because KSP is nothing like that.   Take parts, attach parts, launch parts, land parts, detonate parts, survive falling parts.  KSP is learning through failure.  Unless you go on Youtube and look up the Scott Manley videos, you are going to fail.  You gonna fail bad.  But it's okay.  Failure is only data by another name.  Bit by bit, you'll learn how to do things right.  You'll realize that putting the engines under the tanks is probably a good idea.  Putting the crew capsule in a place not likely to be burned or detonated is also probably a good idea.   Parachutes seem like a logical choice, but what the heck, right?  Maybe you just need a five hundred meter long crumple zone.  Nobody's gonna stop you.  That's the great thing, isn't it?  You can put anything at all you want on the launchpad, and nobody knows well enough to try to stop you.  The Kerbish OSHA rep is permanently locked into the bathroom.  He's not gettin' out of there.  We welded the window shut, locked the door, and put model airplane glue in the keyhole.  Cell phone reception in there is sketchy.  You're safe.  So go nuts.
There's places you can go.  Land at the poles, the sea, the mountains, or all three at once with a creatively timed spray of shrapnel.  There's other worlds.  A big burning thing with no surface that'll tan you for free if you check it out.  It'll tan you to the bone.  So that's a bonus.  There's other worlds.  Red world.  Purple world.  Green world with little worlds around it.  Hidden stuff everywhere.  All of these places are fit to seed with refuse.  Landers, rovers, living quarters, stations, battleships, pasteboard furniture, lawnmowers, spaceplanes, robots, scooters, springboards, et cetera.  KSP is a litterer's dream.  There's so many places you can leave stuff you have no hope of bringing home.
But I've got to warn you.  You've reached TL;DR level four, so here's a bonus.  This game has very unexpected side effects.  You will learn things.  Hoffman transfer.  Periapsis.  Apoapsis.  How orbit actually works.  Why orbit is halfway to anywhere.  Launch windows.  Free transfer windows.  Free returns.  If you make the horrifying inadvertent mistake of buying this game for yourself or your child, somebody's gonna learn things.  It's unavoidable.   Real things, even.  Newton's spectre haunts this game.  You will find no escape, and he fears no earthly garlic.
Lemmie wrap this up for the TL;DR folks who check the bottom summary.  Just get KSP already.  You aren't really learning anything from my review you probably didn't know already.  Let's be honest with each other, here.  Ok?  You don't want to learn whether or not this game is worth buying.  You're looking for someone to make the excuse for you.  You're already gonna get it, you just want someone to possibly take the fall for you if you catch heat for doing it.  And to you, good sirs and madams, I say;  Yes.  Yes, I'll take the blame.  "That fat idiot Whackjob from KSP told me to get the game, or he said he'd cut me."  They'll believe you.  You're good.  So do it.  Hit that buy button.
Thank me later.

I rarely review games. The only other review I have written was of "The Last of Us." This game was also a very well crafted narrative with engrossing characters and environments. The fact that your choices matter draws you even deeper into the story. I would wager that I, as a man in my 30s, am farther from the drama of high school girls than anyone out there. Yet, I was caught up in the story and the relationships. I felt for the characters and wanted to do what I could to ensure the best outcomes for them.
Some have argued that the time travel power makes your decisions feel less impactful, but I find that I found the presence of the power made me more conscious of the choices I was making. After all, it is a game, and in other decision-based games, you make the best choice based on the one or two word descriptor or save the character you like better, and what happens happens. You might go back and play again and make different choices, but then it's hard to remember the choices you made before. This game is compared to other games, like Telltale's Walking Dead, and I see the similarity. However, here the game makes the decision making process part of the story and part of the main character's evolution. I, as the player, felt very much like Max must have. You have the power to change things, so you want to make sure you've made the best possible choice. You still can't really know until much later. It also let's you experiment with different approaches, experience more of the excellent voice acting, explore the characters and their motivations in depth, and get some schadenfreude out of your system to boot! Win win!
*Spoilers ahead*
Ultimately, the game is a fable about unintended consequences. The references to "climate change," which is the unintended consequence of our industrial societies and lifestyles, echo that theme. From the first scene, the game  foreshadows that things are not right in the "space-time contnuum," and it is implied throughout that Max's temporal exploits are having unforeseen repercussions. So the ending, which many found disappointing, fits with that overall theme. I found the ending acceptable, although not perfect. I understand the criticisms of an ending which seems to negate the player's efforts to that point, but I would argue that even if you choose to "undo" what you've done, the nefarious criminals are still brought to justice through the exploits of Max and Chloe throughout the week. Even if, in the end, the week did not "happen," except for Max, it still had meaning for her, and will impact her life and relationships for the rest of her life. She gained confidence and perspective. She came out of her shell, which is also one of the themes driven home repeatedly. It is her story, after all. The final choice is the culmination of her coming of age story about unintended consequences. It cements the point that no matter how much we try to plan and make good choices, ultimately, life is...well...strange.
I would recommend this game for the story, characters, music, and novelty. I have often wished I could turn back time for a few moments to make a better choice, and in this game you can live that.

Garry's Mod is an game that encourages players who bought it to use their creativity and just mess around with multiple assets of the Source Engine. You can also program your own minigames via LUA, and play from others! With endless possibilities and community made content, can Garry's Mod be a good game and worth buying? Let's find out.
Garry's Mod gameplay is diverse and it depends in what the player is currently playing. For example, you have Sandbox Mode, which by the name you just mess around with the tools that the developer(s) gave to you. You can make an scene, building (because of the building tools), and even an hilarious stop motion animation! You can even model your own assets via a third party program (Blender for example), or you can make your scene in-game, and submit it to the Workshop so everyone and you can use it! The possibilities are endless, you the limits are your imagination. Also, did I forgot to mention that you can invite your friends to play together?
Got bored of creating? Well, don't worry because still got
things to try it out that the community had created! There is Prop Hunt, where you are selected to either be an prop, or an hunter. The hunter hunts down the prop players, while the props need to hide and not get caught. You also got Trouble in Terrorist Town, Murder, and more!
When it comes to graphics, instead of comparing today's generation, let's go back to 2004, where the game got released. The graphics
as from Half Life 2, since the game takes things build in the engine and give a portion for the players to use. Comming back to Half Life, at the time, the game's graphics were amazing. But wait! If you own a Source game like Team Fortress 2, you can transfer the maps and assets from it. How cool is that? There is a bit of, let's say, a "graphics change" once you run a TF2 map, but the interface and player model stays the same, with the other assets of the other games. So, since this is a 2004 game, I won't review the graphics.
Optimization by far is one of the most important things to discuss. While the game does contain small specs, so it can run is some potatoes, the game does in fact suffer from some lag. Probably it's my computer, because when I am running simplistic maps, it gets into high FPS. So, it almost depends upon your computer!
Garry's Mod sandbox mode contain a pretty easy self-explanatory gameplay: easy to learn, hard to master, while other gamemodes made by the community offer you a great experience to you and friends. It does in fact lag a little when your computer is considered a bit of a potato in 2017.
- You can make everything you imagine. (+6)
- Endless Game modes and possibilities. (+4)
- FPS drops in simple computers above the recommended specs (-0.5)

Definately worth your money!

I was referred to this game by a friend of mine and I didn't even look at the trailer or screenshots. I had absolutely no idea what to expect.
The INSTANT I finished the first episode, I wanted to play the entire season.
This is one of those games that you really need to have. The story is unbelievably well written, with characters that are superbly developed. Speaking of characters, the jaw-dropping performances of the voice actors will pull you right into the world of Arcadia Bay.
The soundtrack is outstanding! It creates tension when necessary and is vital to the immersive world. I had songs from The Who's Quadrophenia playing in my head at certain points.
"Here by the sea and sand, nothing ever goes as planned..."
About the choices: THEY HAVE CONSEQUENCES! Just trust me on this one. Your choices will change the path of the game, and it's entirely possible to go back and do something differently in the game when you're 3/4 of the way through because you feel nervous or guilty over a previous decision made in the beginning.
Also, just by being 18 at the time of playing it for the first time, it really made the experience feel more authentic to me. You will have a memorable experience even if you're not that age. It does make some of the jokes flow a little smoother.
There are some things that detract from the experience. When combined with the outstanding performances by the voice actors, the lip-syncing just feels off in certain parts. Even though I don't have any major issues with the logic of the game, it's unfortunate that some players feel that it doesn't make sense.
The best advice that I can give is that you should ABSOLUTELY play the first episode. I would also say that the more you put into the game, the more you will get out of it. I know that it's strange to say that about this kind of game, but if you open your mind and use your imagination to put yourself in the footsteps of Max, you will experience a masterpiece of the game. The issues that are in the game do not destroy the experience.
(A little note about the ending: I've seen some reviews that say that the ending is a huge disappointment. Specifically, I've seen reviews that essentially beg for something that isn't given to them. This is where an open mind really counts. The developers emphasize that your own choice is the "right" choice. That goes for EVERY decision in the game. Do what YOU want to do.)

KSP
to sum it up in one acronym and a word KSP is the "WTF simulator" you can either build an accurate close to real life space ship such as one that looks like the Saturn V or you can create some crazy gaint behemoth of a rocket/space plane that could destroy every major city on earth (Earth is called Kerbin on KSP as its a made up solar system (and there are not cities on Kerbin/Earth just your space centre and a tiny air bace on some random island))
Pros
•	The creation of your ship is only limited by your imagination
•	Highly Advanced and technical game would not recommend for people who want a quick and easy game the Phrase “it’s not rocket science” Literally does not apply to this game
•	This game gives you a massive sense of achievement- knowing that your small brain (not an insult just it is small relative to a planet) could put a man (they’re called Kerbal in the game (apologies for the over use of brackets in this review) ) on the Moon a feat that took NASA    $109 billion and  400,000 people to achieve and you have managed to do it with roughly £20, depending on steam price fluctuation I got it for £11, and one computer. You can even do better than NASA and land on other planets many millions of miles away
•	Re-enact Famous NASA missions I have recently Re-enacted the Voyager missions
•	The Games Physics are spot on (I should know I do A-level Physics)
•	Can be quite humorous  sometimes
•	Involves complex thinking makes you feel like a genius
•	has some great mods would definitely recommend  the B9 aerospace mod and the KW rocketry mod you can find these mods either by googleing ‘Kerbal Space Program mods or you can click on the community link at the start of the game it should take you to a website called
•	Graphics are reasonable for an early access game and they can be improved by the mod ‘astronomers visual pack-edge of oblivion’ which really brings some life into the game although I found the install of this mod a little tricky even though there was a how to video on YouTube still took me a couple of hours
•	The Game has a very good sound track the music really does sound ‘spacey’  although it does irritate my family when my volume is turned up
•	Can be applied to real life- as crazy as it sound I have used some of the skills I have learnt in KSP in real life such as how to plan and money management
•	It brings a relief to you parents- My mum and Dad definitely prefer me to play this game than the usual games I play that involve murdering, killing zombies, violence and blood and guts. (although this hasn’t stopped me from playing those games)
•	A very original game not many other games like it out there on steam.
Cons
•	Career mode can be a bit of a grind saving up money and science points to unlock new parts luckily though there is sandbox mode in which everything is unlocked personally I jumped straight to this mode
•	Sandbox mode has a very slightly lower sense of achievement than career mode as you cannot collect science points and as scientific research it the entire point of sending anything into space both on the game and in real life, once the hype of flying to another world and landing there safely wears off you kind of feel the whole mission was a little pointless
•	Sometimes you get the sense the game is trying too hard to be funny and although this can benefit the game it can make the game sound  not very serious and seriousness is something you need when traveling into space
•	It can take a very long time to learn what everything does took me 4 hours to finally get something into space
•	The symmetry tool in rocket and space plane construction although incredibly useful, like the game would be impossible without it, can be a bit dodgy such as pieces will sometimes fit in two places when placed individually i.e. when symmetry is turned off but won’t fit in those same two places when it’s turned on. Luckily 8 time out of 10 this doesn’t happen but when it does it can be annoying
•	Navigation, manoeuvring and timing can all be incredibly hard and frustrating and can take many hours to master. I did not do this but I wish I had, read as many guides and watch as many videos as you can on how to do all the things you want to do in KSP or you will have to do as I did which was spending many hours figuring things out by trial and error
Overall I would give this game a 9/10 and I think it’s a must buy if you want to feel super smart and proud it is my most played game in my Library at the moment and there is no reason why it shouldn’t be yours as well

Let me start off by saying I heard many positive things about this game. I also am from Oregon's Portland area so I feel like this may be marketed towards me a bit more or I have familiarity with Astoria.
Now to the actual game.
I want to say it is well done. That is the art style and aesthetic look is pleasing. The game runs smoothly and I never felt like I missed too much. (some things are just easily missed I think and aren't noticable by the player).
Many of the characters are flat and most options you have with them are very black and white. Which is really how much of the game plays out. you can go left or right. yes or no. up or down. there arent many options that make a real gray area in terms of moral decisions. That being said most characters are boiled down to either being butthurt, ♥♥♥♥♥y, or real dumb.
Its almost like you have to tear an arm off a character before you see them change slightly from their only actual trait. then once the next chapter rolls around they have completely forgotten about how you helped them or the thing you said made them happy.
*Slight Spoilers*
Now, I absolutely hate the logic most people have in this. When you approach the principal and tell him what you saw in the bathroom about a kid with a gun he writes it off as you getting attention. As far I could tell there shouldn't be any reason that this would happen in any school system.
*Theme Spoilers*
I also do not care for the message the game offers. Life is Strange goes into the social commentary of modern? school system. Whether or not this school is a highschool or college is really hard to tell but It has traits of both. So we save a girl's life in the first chapter and we keep having a nightmare about the hurricane or whatever. But by the end when I have been trying to save lives all along the way with this great power, you are given an ultimatum. either I go back and let my "best friend" die. or you let the whole town die. I dont totally agree with the statement it makes. In my opinio this game says that no matter what you do to save this person, they were MEANT to die, this "butterfly" effect makes a hurricane wipe out the whole town. This really bothers me too because you actually can save another character from committing suicide and it kind of cheapens the experience of saving her...
Anyways I did play all the way through but I felt like the writing was poor and I wanted to get more out this game. Dont pay more than 3 dollars for this if you really want to experience it for yourself.

This has been my favorite game for almost a year now.  If my Steam account got lost somehow, I would buy it again. As a long-time MechWarrior fan, lacking any decent single player title these days, KSP satisfies my desire to: imagine a thing, composed of specific parts, and with a mission objective in mind; build that thing, identify obstacles to building it, overcome them, make the thing pleasing to the eye; then launch my creation, (hopefully) perform the objective(s) without blowing up, and finally returning home. Of course missions rarely succeed on the first try, but that's where re-tweaking comes into play. I spend more time in the creation phase than actually playing my missions, which is perfectly fine by me.
Recent updates to this game are taking it from full-on sandbox with player imagined goals and no restrictions, to something with a little more structure and direction complete with finance limitations. Full sandbox mode is still available though, if you prefer. The newer AI generated missions are fun and lead you out of comfort zones, giving you a greater skill-set. Replay-ability is absolutely part of this game and you can expect to look forward to starting all over time and again.
*edit* Now that we're in Beta, this game is even better than my original review. These guys are doing it right. If you even remotely think you might like this type of game, stop reading reviews and go try the demo. Then be prepared to talk yourself into buying it. It's gonna happen. If you have willpower, catching a 40% off sale is as good a deal as they offer for this one.

This has been my favorite game for almost a year now.  If my Steam account got lost somehow, I would buy it again. As a long-time MechWarrior fan, lacking any decent single player title these days, KSP satisfies my desire to: imagine a thing, composed of specific parts, and with a mission objective in mind; build that thing, identify obstacles to building it, overcome them, make the thing pleasing to the eye; then launch my creation, (hopefully) perform the objective(s) without blowing up, and finally returning home. Of course missions rarely succeed on the first try, but that's where re-tweaking comes into play. I spend more time in the creation phase than actually playing my missions, which is perfectly fine by me.
Recent updates to this game are taking it from full-on sandbox with player imagined goals and no restrictions, to something with a little more structure and direction complete with finance limitations. Full sandbox mode is still available though, if you prefer. The newer AI generated missions are fun and lead you out of comfort zones, giving you a greater skill-set. Replay-ability is absolutely part of this game and you can expect to look forward to starting all over time and again.
*edit* Now that we're in Beta, this game is even better than my original review. These guys are doing it right. If you even remotely think you might like this type of game, stop reading reviews and go try the demo. Then be prepared to talk yourself into buying it. It's gonna happen. If you have willpower, catching a 40% off sale is as good a deal as they offer for this one.

KSP is, without a doubt, the best early-access game out right now.
Reasons why:
• Constantly being updated
• One of the best modding communities out there
• Only 30 dollars
• An entire solar system filled with Planets and Moons to explore
• Even if this game somehow gets abandoned by the developers, it still has enough content to justify it.(unlike most early access games)
• You can use your own imagination to create the vehicles you want.
• Even thought it has "Space Program" in the name, it's not only locked to space crafts. You can build cars, planes, boats, helicopters, etc.
• (For the most part) Realistic physics.
• Full sized planets.
• Career mode.
• Sandbox mode.
• You can transport asteroids...
The only cons I could think of:
• No variety in Kerbal appearances, unless you use mods.
• Physics become glitchy when you speed up time.
This game is definately worth the 30 dollars, and is better than most games today, especially early-access games.

Life is strange is honestly one of the most strenuous games to play. Not only is it stressful on your head, but you get so attached to the characters it feels as if you really are the character. Life is strange is a story based game, and  is very easy to get attached to. Every choice you make, will either make a good thing happen or a bad thing happen. This being on your head makes it very stressful.
You play as a young adult named Max Caulfield. After moving to Seattle from her little town Arcadia Oregon,  she returns to go to Blackwell acadamy,  a school for art. After having a vission, Max is very disturbed in her classroom setting. After leaving class, she witnesses something very disturbing and discovers she can rewind time. After discovering this power. Max and her childhood best friend, Chloe, go on an adventure for what Max beleives will be saving the end of the world. During this adventure, you will meet amazing characters some of which you will hate, and some of which you will love. But every one leaves behind tough choices that can affect the outcome of the game. In the end, there is always a tough choice that you will either regret or love.
Life is Strange is so mentally intense that after the end of each chapter the creator says "If you feel this game has harmed you in anyway, please contact us and we will find you a support group near your location" or around the lines of that. Honestly, when I played life is strange I started to tear up a million times, and the last time that happened was the end of red dead redepmtion, and we all know what happens there ;). But legit, Life is Strange will leave you with a♥♥♥♥♥♥ton of emotions, it could be anger, sadness or a mixture of both. When I played i learned many lessons, and I feel this game has made me a better person mentally. After having doubted for a long time I decided to buy this game in the summersale, and I wasn't dissapointed. I had seen many people saying this game was the best they had ever played, and I have to agree that it is one of the better games I have played. It is indeed an emotional rollercoaster.
Pro's:
- I really like the art style.
- Good story, with likable characters.
- There were some unexpected twists (for me atleast), and one of them really broke my heart...
- You (can) get really attached to the characters, which sucks at times (as you'll experience for yourself once you play it), but it is also again a sign of good writing.
- As said before, this game is really good at playing with your emotions (Yes, I cried...a lot). So, be prepared ;)
- Nice soundtrack
Neutral:
- The game starts with an introduction of the characters, which are the stereotypical teenagers you'll find in American high shool films/tv series. I thought that was a bit cheap. Later on, as you get to know each character better, the stereotypical thing isn't so bad anymore, hence the neutral point.
- The teenagers are really 'edgy' with a lot of cursing. I personlly don't mind cursing in games, but this was a bit much and unnecessary at times.
- A lot of people are complaining that the choises you make during the game don't matter in the end. If you have seen Final Destination, you'll know that you can't escape your fate. So for me the ending made perfect sense, but I can understand that you don't like the final choise.
- The lipsyncing of the characters was a bit off sometimes.
- Episode 5 was a bit lengthy, it often felt like filler material to me to get it to the same length as the previous episodes. But the ending is worth it though ;)
Con's:
- The autosave function sometimes had really long periods between saves, so if you needed to stop you had to choose between getting late or playing everyting over again from the last saving point the next time. I didn't really like that.
- The controls for PC were really oaf. You have to hold and drag to choose the option you want, but a lot of times this didn't work/respond as it should have. I had to drag the mouse almost off the table sometimes to finally get it to respond. This made me angry at times, which resulted in loosing the immersion of the game.
Overall a pretty good game, but the controls could have been better, so I would rate this game 8/10

SPOILERS FOR THE OPENING OF EPISODE ONE:
As a fan of several Telltale games and the likes of Oxenfree, I decided to give the, now free, Life Is Strange Ep1 a shot.
And to its credit, it opened promising a choice-based decision game with a healthy mix of Majoras Mask and Prince of Persia time mechanics in a Donnie Darko-esque scenario.
Unfortunately, nowhere in Ep1 is the promise delivered upon.
Pivotal player-choice moments fail to provide logical selections, instead choosing to force the player down several restrictive storylines empty of any common-sense or practicality.
Your ability to time-travel is inconsistent and infuriously primarily locked behind puzzle moments, when it could be used as an extremely inticing mechanic for decision making- rather than gimmicks.
The characters introduced are cringy at best and inherantly offputting at worst, making it extremely hard to care about, or even believe their dilemmas.
Voice acting, aesthetic and premise are the only elements of this game worth praising.
Due to the love Life Is Strange has recieved it is possible the game begins to succeed in later episodes, but Episode One has failed to give me a reason to further on and I am greatful no money needed to be spent for this to come to my attention.

Not for the weak of souls. There are many steps of progress, and beating each one of them gives a feeling of accomplishment that no other game can give you. The steps are as following:
1. Create a craft that does not implode when it's put on the launch pad. (Struts, aka SUPER SPACE DUCT TAPE)
2. Return to the Vehicle Assembly Building and add engines.
3. Launch UPWARDS. You do not want to travel downwards, that is very bad, especielly for your pilot.
4. Actually get up in the air in one piece.
This is where the game starts to give you multiple options. You can either try to reach space, or return to the ground. Sometimes the latter happens no matter what you want, and it happens very fast.
5. If you are travelling downwards, this is a good time to remember that you forgor parachutes.
6. If you came this far, congratulations! You have now reached space.
7. You see Kerbin down below? No, it's not getting bigger, you are just accelerating towards it. Burn prograde and establish a safe orbit ABOVE the atmosphere!
8. Sorry, you've run out of fuel, and the poor astronaut is now stuck in space forever.
9. Got a new craft up with more fuel? Great, start travelling towards the Mun.
10. Yeah, you're not supposed to faceplant in the Mun, please try again.
11. Get close to the Mun, then burn retrograde and get into an orbit.
12. Recalculate your fuel, it's probably better to deorbit and smash into the mun than being stuck in orbit forever. Atleast it'll make nice fireworks...
13. Start deorbiting. If you are lucky, you will have enough fuel to land, otherwise, please think about a name for the new crater now.
14. You are now successfully accelerating in a "controlled" manner towards the surface of the Mun. I recommend you to start breaking soon.
15. Touchdown! You didn't need that one enginge anyways, right? Oh, you wanted to return home.. Well, take Jeb out for a stroll on his new pet rock and prepare a rescue mission.
16. Design a craft that is capable of saving Jeb from the Mun.
17. Yeah, this new craft isn't stable... Please start over from step 1 until you are able to launch it.
18. Rinse and repeat.

Easily one of the most unique and challenging games I've ever played. It feels so rewarding when you finally learn to get a kerbal to the mun and beyond.
The devs work very hard, constantly releasing new content as they work towards their magnificent end goal. The sandbox portion of the game can be somewhat overwhelming to new players, as the sheer number of parts available can be scary. However, the ever-growing career mode is shaping up to be everything I could dream of.
In career mode, you start off with only a few basic parts, and as you gather scientific data by conducting tests throughout the solar system, you can unlock more efficient and useful parts to build your montrous ships. Money recently added a new aspect in this mode, as you complete contracts with sponsors ranging from "Try out our new prototype part while orbiting the Mun" to "Save our poor lost astronaut!". The career mode is starting to really feel like you're managing a complex space program, instead of just launching poor astronauts to their deaths (although if that is your thing, this game has seen many, many tests go wrong).
If you are someone who loves games involving resource management and creativity (Age of Empires, Rollercoaster Tycoon, Minecraft even), I would highly reccomend this to you. The only downside to this game is the harsh learning curve, but what I've found is all the games worth my time don't hold your hand. My first couple flights in this game remind me of my first night in minecraft: I had no idea what I was doing, and a copious amount of death was involved. Most of your great designs and ideas won't work, but when you do find one that works, I can't describe the feeling of accomplishment.

As a bearded, manly, manly man, I can openly admit: This game made me cry like a little kid!
No matter what kind of games (or stories) you are into, whether you like grand strategy, shooters, or puzzle games. (This game is none of that, but) I can guarantee YOU WILL LOVE IT! Please give  Episode 1 a try for free and get sucked right in to this intense story. I could barely wait the download time of the other Episodes, once I was finished with the first.
The story of this game is amazing in every way I can think of. The characters are deep and develop SO WELL! I myself felt like I bonded with these characters and had a tough time putting them trough difficult situations. Nothing you do goes unnoticed. Every choice you make genuinely makes a difference. (Some more than others, but the point stands). Whilst the actual endings of the game do not differ massively, the way there will always be a bit of a different experience, making different choices along the way.
The gameplay also works very well. I played the game with an X-Box 360 controller and the controls worked very smoothely. In the many hours I played this game (I played all the way trough it over the course of one weekend) I only noticed one little problem with the gameplay, which was mostly due to me screwing up massively and was an easy fix, by reloading the last checkpoint (which was very fairly placed at that).
The main mechanic of this game is messing around with time, by rewinding it and I can tell you two things:
1. This game will suck up your free-time like a vacuum cleaner sucks dust of your dirty gamer-bedroom-floor
AND
2. After you have finished the game you are going to wish you could rewind to a point in time, when you had not yet played the game so you could experience it all over again.

After having doubted for a long time I decided to buy this game in the summersale, and I wasn't dissapointed. I had seen many people saying this game was the best they had ever played, and I have to agree that it is one of the better games I have played. It is indeed an emotional rollercoaster.
Pro's:
- I really like the art style.
- Good story, with likable characters.
- There were some unexpected twists (for me atleast), and one of them really broke my heart...
- You (can) get really attached to the characters, which sucks at times (as you'll experience for yourself once you play it), but it is also again a sign of good writing.
- As said before, this game is really good at playing with your emotions (Yes, I cried...a lot). So, be prepared ;)
- Nice soundtrack
Neutral:
- The game starts with an introduction of the characters, which are the stereotypical teenagers you'll find in American high shool films/tv series. I thought that was a bit cheap. Later on, as you get to know each character better, the stereotypical thing isn't so bad anymore, hence the neutral point.
- The teenagers are really 'edgy' with a lot of cursing. I personlly don't mind cursing in games, but this was a bit much and unnecessary at times.
- A lot of people are complaining that the choises you make during the game don't matter in the end. If you have seen Final Destination, you'll know that you can't escape your fate. So for me the ending made perfect sense, but I can understand that you don't like the final choise.
- The lipsyncing of the characters was a bit off sometimes.
- Episode 5 was a bit lengthy, it often felt like filler material to me to get it to the same length as the previous episodes. But the ending is worth it though ;)
Con's:
- The autosave function sometimes had really long periods between saves, so if you needed to stop you had to choose between getting late or playing everyting over again from the last saving point the next time. I didn't really like that.
- The controls for PC were really oaf. You have to hold and drag to choose the option you want, but a lot of times this didn't work/respond as it should have. I had to drag the mouse almost off the table sometimes to finally get it to respond. This made me angry at times, which resulted in loosing the immersion of the game.
Overall a pretty good game, but the controls could have been better, so I would rate this game 8/10

A game has never invoked such a wide range of emotions from me as Kerbal Space Program. Each baby step that started with me blowing up rockets on the launch pad, to getting my first rocket into orbit, and ultimately taking a giant leap for all Kerbal-kind by stepping foot onto the Mun! All of those moments brought with them an overwhelming feeling of accomplishment.
I remember when an unsuccessful aerobrake in Jool’s atmosphere left poor Bob, Bill, and Jebediah Kerman plummeting to their doom... a sense of fear and dread washed over me. As if I was watching cherished loved ones in their final moments. I had to reload my previous save because it was too much. It may sound incredibly silly to anyone who’s not passionate about this game but eventually nothing becomes more important than protecting Jeb’s life.
If you love astronomy, or just look up to the stars with wonder and curiosity. You know who you are, the person who has watched every episode of Star Trek, someone who can quote Carl Sagan word for word. You’re the person who stays up to 2 o’clock in the morning to see a rover land successfully on Mars. You’re a dreamer. Or perhaps, like me, you were just too lazy and stupid to become an astronaut… if any of those describe you, this is your game. Brace yourself for the emotional roller coaster.

Really was a beautiful emotional poignant game- I definitely reccomend it. The animation was overall very good aside from the faces that were very stiff and unmoving which took me out of the story at times.
My biggest issue with this game was how tropey and unrealistic it was as far as a typical high schoolers life in a small town in the north west would be. Max had very little happening with her personality throughout the game, yet was inexplicably the target of bullying (which was revealed to be out of jealousy) and an intense friendship with Chloe (who was incredibly cool and edgy and was bursting with personality). Max's character felt like the creators wanted a blank canvas that the players of the game who fit that "alernative nerd" feeling and who lacked any sense of style whatsoever (like ENOUGH with the neat girly little graphic t shirts... ) could self insert themselves into and live vicariously in Arcadia Bay as Max. "Victoria the bully" and her clique also reminded me of a representation of high schoolers on a disney channel show from the early 2000s where the wealthy beautiful popular talented girl is jealous of the quiet wallflower who rarely talked to her or anyone for that matter for some reason. I found myself scoffing at the idea of this girl finding the need to relentlessly and loudly make snide comments in class about this reserved girl. Also why was Mr. Jefferson so into her photography and entering her work in the contest?? Like Chill OUT (and i mean that in multiple ways).
The story itself was interesting and again, there were touching moments and multiple times where the decision you had to make was such a catch 22 that it left you trying to figure out the right choice when of course there wasn't one. I found myself actually sobbing at a section of episode 2 i think.. (maybe it was 3?) and the super simple "choose your own adventure" but better format was really nice and allowed you to sit back for a majority of the game and watch your choices play out. This game is going to be tough to decide whether or not to replay because one one hand I really want to see what changes would be made based on what different decisions are made... on the other hand the long unskippable speaking scenes that drag out because of slow clear talking and large pauses between sentences would make a replay drag out far longer than I'd want.
Overall, I highly recommend this game and suggest that you just prepare yourself to get past the annoying trope ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t to get the real heart of the game.

For something so seemingly simple, the hours upon hours that I've spent playing this game reveal the true genius of KSP: blowing stuff up never gets old.
Kerbal Space Program: the sandbox rocket simulation game that will teach you more about orbital mechanics than you thought there was to know, all while killing countless Kerbals, and having a right-good-time doing it. That's KSP in a nut-shell. Lots of bugs, but the game is so darned fun I keep coming back and starting over anyway, and it's only at version 0.24 while I write this, so there should be a mountain more content and bugs-squished before release.
The core gameplay consists of snapping together prefab rocket parks, then simulating their functions in the Kerbal Universe. The game, while it does have some bugs, actually makes rocket engineering pretty darned easy, truth be told. It's an impressive feat of programming. Then, once you begin a simulation, you're unwittingly learning about atmospheric drag, orbital mechanics, and the law of diminishing returns.
I can honestly say, this is quite possibly my favourite video game ever. Kudos SQUAD, please keep up the great work!
-- Post-release edit --
While there are still some annoying bugs in KSP (craft that veer left or right because...???) the core game mechanics have been maintained such that my Early Access review still stands. Favourite game ever.

A game has never invoked such a wide range of emotions from me as Kerbal Space Program. Each baby step that started with me blowing up rockets on the launch pad, to getting my first rocket into orbit, and ultimately taking a giant leap for all Kerbal-kind by stepping foot onto the Mun! All of those moments brought with them an overwhelming feeling of accomplishment.
I remember when an unsuccessful aerobrake in Jool’s atmosphere left poor Bob, Bill, and Jebediah Kerman plummeting to their doom... a sense of fear and dread washed over me. As if I was watching cherished loved ones in their final moments. I had to reload my previous save because it was too much. It may sound incredibly silly to anyone who’s not passionate about this game but eventually nothing becomes more important than protecting Jeb’s life.
If you love astronomy, or just look up to the stars with wonder and curiosity. You know who you are, the person who has watched every episode of Star Trek, someone who can quote Carl Sagan word for word. You’re the person who stays up to 2 o’clock in the morning to see a rover land successfully on Mars. You’re a dreamer. Or perhaps, like me, you were just too lazy and stupid to become an astronaut… if any of those describe you, this is your game. Brace yourself for the emotional roller coaster.

In all my years of being an avid RPG, story-loving based gamer. I have never found a game so close to home. The reality of it, the consequences of your actions representing your past,present and future. Its what makes who you are. This game drives that point so close, you can actually see that the sci-fi elements were just to make it fun, and that the real problems were somethings that everyone goes through. Being insecure, unloved, hated, bullied, not knowing everything, It's as if the game was reality for those 13-18 hours. Although there was no really RPG elements to it, the story was awesome. I already predicted who the main villain was, and found the romance in it sub-par and yet It doesnt matter. The meaning behind this game is what makes it so special. This game teaches you to be yourself, that you should be proud and never go back or look back without smiles, tears, or anger. without breaks. This game might be more expensive that some other titles or less than the big ones (Fallout, Witcher) but for anyone who loves a good story and wants to experience a glimpse of what makes life worth living. Get the game from episode 1-5. It was really worth it to me. This game got me laughing, crying, cursing and wishing that the developers would make another game just like it.

After seeing a lot of Gmod Idiot Box, Half Life Robot Chicken, and other kinds of humorous Gmod videos on Youtube, I have had the urge to purchase this game for years to enjoy it for myself. The first few hours into playing, my friend and I enter one of the popular RP servers. We start off by changing our job title to "Black Lives Matter Protestors", we run around annoying the cops in the game by shouting "BLACK LIVES MATTER!" while the cops chase after us armed with batons and guns attempting to attack and shoot us while shouting racial slurs. After that I entered a hotel and the hotel owner was typing in a code on a keypad to enter the restricted part of the hotel as I snuck up behind him and managed to enter the restricted area by sneaking right behind him. I found this room that he had which consisted of money printers and I camped in that room remaining hiddden as I picked up thousands of dollars worth of bills till the printers were empty of resources to continue making the money. After collecting my newfound wealth I snuck back out of the hotel and exited into the streets where this one guy created a box that drops AK47s underneath it after paying the cost of the rifle first. This one player pays the box which dropped an AK47, and I snuck up with my grav gun and snatched the AK47 for myself while the player remains clueless where the rifle disappeared to. I sit back and watch the player flip out on the guy that created the gun spawning box calling him a scammer/cheat over microphone. I leave as the scene gets much more intense only for some gangster to follow me and attempted to mug me in the middle of the street. I draw my stolen AK47 on the gangster who reacts in shock and attempts to escape only to get gunned down by me. I just started playing this recently and I already look forward to the mayhem I plan on causing in the future! >=D

Great game, has provided me tons of entertainment. The devs in this game are miles ahead of many other independent gamedevs, and it definitely seems like they care about the final product. No DLC crap either! The entire game is right there for you after you've bought it, which is pretty refreshing nowadays.
Out of the box, there are tons of parts as well as seven planets (Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Ceres, Jupiter, and Pluto analogues, along with moons for many of them). There are many mods out there that add new parts, change up the UI, overhaul gameplay, add new planets, and even add new solar systems to visit. They're very simple to install; most of the times, you're just dragging and dropping one or two folders.
The best part about this game, though, is that it really helps introduce you to the basics of orbital mechanics. I'd installed other spaceflight sims like Orbiter (it's a much more realistic, hardcore spaceflight simulator) without having any real idea what I was doing; after playing around in this game for a few weeks, I was able to go back to that and finally understand what was going on.

Garry's Mod is a sandbox game. No objectives, no goals, it just provides you with the tools and allows you do whatever please. However it's beyond that, since there's the Steam Workshop..which is likely what your fun will come out of the most. Maps, models, more tools, gamemodes, etc.
GMod also comes with "Trouble in Terrorist Town", or TTT for short. Basically you either hunt down all the Terrorists or kill all the civilians, and etc depending on your role.
As for me, I mainly play on "Ultimate Chimera Hunt", which is a "Hide and Seek" gamemode based off of the game Mother 3.
There are two things to watch out for: you'll need to have the resource files for both Team Fortress 2 and Counter Strike: Source in order to
enjoy the game and not have missing textures on most maps, which means two long game downloads and 20$ down the drain for a "dead" game and some resources.
There are also the achievements, which are very time consuming. "Very" can hardly describe how long these achievements can take.
Regardless, I find the 10$ price tag worth it if you look at how much you can get out of it and the fun shenanigans that can be pulled with friends.

tl;dr: this game is perfect. play it
I would describe Life Is Strange as a choice-based interactive story. While its still very much a video game, I view it as more of an experience. Playing through it is a journey. This is one of the most intense story-driven games I've played. Its one of those titles you can really get into and obsess over even after completing it. A lot of the events and sequences that take place throughout the game are very dramatic, intense, and just beautiful - even the negative ones.
Beauty is something Life Is Strange doesn't fall short of. The atmosphere, the environments, and the characters are all filled with so much polish and depth. I found myself completely pulled in and immersed during my time playing it.
The actual gameplay consists of you wandering around different playfields, viewing and interacting with random objects, and talking to characters while always being allowed to make choices in dialogue and action. There are a few situations where you have to do some specific objectives, but they aren't too common. If you take your time and really explore everything, your playthrough will actually last a while. Its the kind of game where I felt like interacting with every single object and talking to every character was a pleasure rather than a chore. My first go through the game took me 13 hours which is actually pretty good.
I'm not going to spoil any of the story. I think its better go in without any expectations or knowledge of it. All I can really say is its wonderfully wrote - even if it does seem a little cliche at times. Don't let that turn you off, it ends up with a lot of excitement and twists. Plus almost every choice actually does have an effect on later events. Sometimes these effects are subtle and sometimes large. I really love this about the game and it made me immediately start a second playthrough after to try some of the other choices.
It was also something I couldn't put down once starting. This game is filled with immersive qualities and will really keep your focus. One thing I really have to praise is how much personality the characters had. This isn't a game where I can't remember anyone's name but the lead character. I knew the characters very well all throughout. Even in their mobile text messages, they're so real and full of life. I really love how well they captured the image of everyone and at times it was even impressive.
The visuals in this game aren't really anything special from a technical standpoint, but it has a unique artstyle and I loved it. While it isn't very realistic, but it isn't too caroony either. There's a really nice blend and the game looks very smooth. At times, the environments can almost look like paintings. A great example of how a realistic setting can be gorgeous without AAA graphical quality.
The music is pretty incredible as well. A lot of music may just play in the background, but plenty of it was very memorable. I found myself listening to numerous tracks outside of the game. Garry's Mod is a sandbox game. No objectives, no goals, it just provides you with the tools and allows you do whatever please. However it's beyond that, since there's the Steam Workshop..which is likely what your fun will come out of the most. Maps, models, more tools, gamemodes, etc.
GMod also comes with "Trouble in Terrorist Town", or TTT for short. Basically you either hunt down all the Terrorists or kill all the civilians, and etc depending on your role.
As for me, I mainly play on "Ultimate Chimera Hunt", which is a "Hide and Seek" gamemode based off of the game Mother 3.
There are two things to watch out for: you'll need to have the resource files for both Team Fortress 2 and Counter Strike: Source in order to
enjoy the game and not have missing textures on most maps, which means two long game downloads and 20$ down the drain for a "dead" game and some resources.
There are also the achievements, which are very time consuming. "Very" can hardly describe how long these achievements can take.
Regardless, I find the 10$ price tag worth it if you look at how much you can get out of it and the fun shenanigans that can be pulled with friends.

Garrys Mod was one of the first games I played when I built my PC. Since then, I've had a blast learning how to use addons and make my own creations. In a nutshell, Garrys Mod is literally a game inside a game, a creation tool or even just a hangout for friends. I started off playing alone to learn the basics (It's not as difficult as most think!) of the game and view what it really had to offer.
I'm a sucker for Valve games and knowing that you can import files from most, if not all of those games, made me really happy. I will note if you plan to play any online modes or use most addons, I suggest to have a few games in your library to import.
An example of said games: Half-Life 2 and Counter-Strike Source are usually two good games to have before delving into Garrys Mod. I'd personally recommend buying the Valve Games Pack when it goes on sale. It gives you close to all of Valves games and boy is it a great deal on sale! A must buy if you fall in love with Garrys Mod.
Some may ask how is the community? Well, that's a case by case basis. I've had servers where the entire group of people were just awesome to talk to and play with. Then you have the occasional screaming kid or adult (Yes, really) because they got killed in a game mode or feel it's unfair. Don't let the community throw you off of this awesome game though!

All in all I adore this game. It's got a nice bit of singleplayer fun, multiplayer mayhem and some amazingly fun modding tools. Plus, you can't beat that price! See you in game!

After 1000 hours of this game, which is about me playing 41 whole days of this game, I thought it was time to write a review for this game since I rarely get so immersed in a game in which to a point where I get 100 hours in a game let alone 1000.
-  I'm sure there are many differing opinions here, but from my experience, a good deal of servers are filled with nice, and funny people.
- A huge amount of addons to choose from. Skins, guns, vehicles, drugs, and much more to test with.
- Obviously this is subjective, so if you're a graphics ♥♥♥♥♥ this could be a con, but if you're like me with an awful computer you can most likely run this game.
- There are so many people you can meet on servers, adding one or two onto your profile can help you jerk your ego! Personally, all of my friends I met on Garry's Mod
- There is a wide range of gamemodes you can choose from such as DarkRP, TTT (Personal Favorite), Prop Hunt, (insert thousands of other rp servers), ect. and to go with the gamemodes you have hundreds of servers to choose from. Saddly, lesser known gamemodes will be rejected, and there will not be as many servers to choose from.
- I got this game from a friend, we were looking for a game we could play together. Many of the hours I have, came from me and my friend just screwing around on sandbox and the addons.
- Not that much of a problem for most people, you most likely can handle a few♥♥♥♥♥♥♥here and there. Theres a few cheaters (ghosters, ect.), hackers (only have seen one since I've been playing), and one or one hundred 12 year olds (though alot of squeakers aren't THAT bad). But I think the good people outweigh the bad.
- Both of those games you should probably consider buying yourself, but if you don't want to, theres nothing you can do (legally) to get those textures. You practically need these textures to play any TTT server or dark rp. But like I said, if you have the heart to somehow get the textures otherwise, you can eliminate this con.
This game really does not have any cons, so if you have 10$ laying around, this should definitly be the game you get.

Life Is Strange is a Episodic title developed by Dontnod Entertainment, and sees you take control of Maxine Caulfield, a twelfth grade student of Blackwell Academy, a school in the fictional Oregonian town of Arcadia Bay. I'll try to keep plot details to a minimum, and there will not be any spoilers in this review.
LiS consists of 5 episodes, with each episode more or less covering an in-game day, all surrounding the journey of Max as she, an 18 year old senior, copes with the prospect of adulthood and leaving her childhood, while reminiscing of it as she's reintroduced to elements and people from it.
The game sees the player take control of Max, who, after discovering she has the power to turn back time, starts experiencing strange things in Arcadia Bay, all reaching climax by Episode 5. I won't get into too many plot details and what you just read didn't spoil anything major for you.
In my opinion, the game is a masterful blend of storytelling, character development, music, and symbolism. The game makes sure to utilize every episode best as possible to develop character personalities and relationships to maximize the story's affect on both character and player as the plot unfolds more greatly throughout Episodes 3, 4, and 5.
The game is an incredible work of art, and an exceptional example of how videogames have just as much an ability to be real works of art as other forms of modern media, such as film and music. The game's ability to make characters real and to make characters matter to the audience is a crucial part of why any game or piece of art should be able to function on a basic level, and LiS is dutifully able to have characters relate and connect with the audience, and in turn succeeds in making the player care about the plight of the characters.
The game has exceptional usage of licensed music, with tracks from artists such as Amanda Palmer and Angus & Julia Stone put in perfectly fitting moments of the game. What is composed for the game by Jonathan Morali of the French band Syd Matters, is beautifully used to convey emotions of any type the game demands and the player feels, from love to loss, to anger and fear, to even longing and reminiscence. The game aptly uses music as a tool to connect with the player, and as such, becomes an even stronger title.
In short, I suggest you try Episode 1 - which is free- out for a spin if you're new to of LiS. If you like it, I strongly suggest you buy the rest of them, you will not be disappointed in the slight; this game is a shining beacon of an example of art in the form of new media, and for videogames, in spite of what many have said in the past, to be examples of art in our culture.

This game is like being in an immersive interactive movie and it hits you in the feels a lot.. It definetly is catered to the current generation of coming to age kids, but you can still relate and fall in love with the story and characters even if you're older. The story is wonderfully told, and the soundtrack compliments the atmosphere and tone of everything perfectly. I felt like I was playing a chick flick movie or Tumblr: The Movie at times, but once you look past some of the stereotypes and hipster stuff it really is a very enjoyable experience..
I've always been a fan of movies with time paradox like Back to the Future, The Butterfly Effect, Project Almanac and such.. The themes are similar, and the consequence of having the power to alter time will have an impact big or small on the future. I had a heavy Butterfly Effect vibe throughout the majority of the game, due to the dynamic of the story being told and the drama that unfolds being very similar.
The fact you can't just go back and load a new save makes the decision making process much better, you have to go with your gut on what you think Max would do.. That's another thing, you really find yourself thinking like Max would think, not so much what you personally would think and that really added to the immersiveness of the game for me.
While I felt the game could of been a bit longer and Episode 5 could of been a bit less rushed, the character development and experience really gives that a pass.. It's been a long time since I've been able to care for minor characters in a game until playing this. Every decision you make you wonder what it will change as the story goes on, and leaves you wondering if it was the right choice.
My only real gripe is even though your decision making does impact the story, there are actually only two endings and your decisions made throughout the game don't really impact those endings at all. I do wish there were numerous endings, or at least 3-4 tops just to give some variety based on your choices.. (I guess the Witcher 3 spoiled me with the amount of different endings you could of had) That also kind of takes away from replay value a bit as well, I can maybe see myself having a second playthrough just to try different things and do the alternate ending but then that would be it.
Overall though this is worth the price, and with Episode 1 being free to play it's worth checking out to see if you can get into the game before you purchase the rest of the episodes.

I can't recommend this game enough.  While still technically under development, the game is in a form most indie titles would consider "complete".  I would recommend starting in sandbox mode as the game has a little bit of a learning curve, but once you figure out how to get into orbit, the game gets very fun, not to mention that crashing spectacularly has it's own draw.  There is a very active modding community, providing endless replayability, and while I would normally say "play through the vanilla game before installing mods", in this case it's not only easy mod, simply drop the mod folder into the data folder, but the mods only make the base game better without detracting from anything, so mod away.  There are fairly regular substantive updates from the developers and they actually listen to their customers.  The only thing I could want for at this time is a multiplayer mode, if only the timescale syncing could be addressed.  Easily a 10/10.
Update:  Still one of the best games out there.  Supportive developers and lots of mods for an easy-going sit-back-and-enjoy-space game.

I cannot recommend this game enough. I purchased it way before it was on steam and have spent a good portion of my life exploring the solar system and I can say it was time well spent. The feeling of accomplishment when you set out to do something you see as impossible and finally succeed is unsurpassed by most games of any genre. The learning curve is very steep, but that is a good thing. You can plan a mission to explore the surface of another world just to get there and realize that you forgot to put a ladder on your vessel or use to much fuel and the whole thing fails and waste hours of time. But that is what makes this game so special. The trial and error, the testing, the variations and changes you make to your rockets will change as you progress to achieve your goals. You can waste hours just building contraptions that you know will fail and have fun watching the mayhem ensue. I have had feelings of accomplishment and failure with this game that I find impossible to match in many ways with any game. Fly safe or don't you'll still have a blast!

Life is strange has definitely become my favourite game. I think it’s the best of any choice & consequence types of games even though I really enjoyed Beyond Two Souls and many games by Telltale. Absolutely worth the full price and more, and now that the first episode is free there’s no excuse to not try it.
There’s many great reviews about the story, themes, characters and everything, so I try to not repeat too much of that.
Though some of the characters are quite stereotypical there’s almost always some depth to them and not everything is what it seems at first. Many characters feel very real and alive. Voice acting, sounds and soundtrack are really good. The graphic style is really nice; it doesn’t attempt to be photo realistic, but it translates atmosphere in every setting perfectly, with the lighting, details and colour scheme so good I can feel even temperature and scents (maybe that’s too much).
it has a lot of replay value. At least for me, I keep wanting to play it again and again. I think the game has something for everyone.
The game itself has a lot of blatant nostalgia tripping (love it), but mostly aspects of contemporary life, with social media and memes and whatnot. In a way it might not age ”well”, when so much of it is connected to today (think of TV shows and films from 80’s/90’s showing off cutting edge technology of that time which feel ridiculous by today’s standards). Then again in the future it’s going to be quite a priceless time capsule of some aspects of today’s life, in a game form.

This game is like being in an immersive interactive movie and it hits you in the feels a lot.. It definetly is catered to the current generation of coming to age kids, but you can still relate and fall in love with the story and characters even if you're older. The story is wonderfully told, and the soundtrack compliments the atmosphere and tone of everything perfectly. I felt like I was playing a chick flick movie or Tumblr: The Movie at times, but once you look past some of the stereotypes and hipster stuff it really is a very enjoyable experience..
I've always been a fan of movies with time paradox like Back to the Future, The Butterfly Effect, Project Almanac and such.. The themes are similar, and the consequence of having the power to alter time will have an impact big or small on the future. I had a heavy Butterfly Effect vibe throughout the majority of the game, due to the dynamic of the story being told and the drama that unfolds being very similar.
The fact you can't just go back and load a new save makes the decision making process much better, you have to go with your gut on what you think Max would do.. That's another thing, you really find yourself thinking like Max would think, not so much what you personally would think and that really added to the immersiveness of the game for me.
While I felt the game could of been a bit longer and Episode 5 could of been a bit less rushed, the character development and experience really gives that a pass.. It's been a long time since I've been able to care for minor characters in a game until playing this. Every decision you make you wonder what it will change as the story goes on, and leaves you wondering if it was the right choice.
My only real gripe is even though your decision making does impact the story, there are actually only two endings and your decisions made throughout the game don't really impact those endings at all. I do wish there were numerous endings, or at least 3-4 tops just to give some variety based on your choices.. (I guess the Witcher 3 spoiled me with the amount of different endings you could of had) That also kind of takes away from replay value a bit as well, I can maybe see myself having a second playthrough just to try different things and do the alternate ending but then that would be it.
Overall though this is worth the price, and with Episode 1 being free to play it's worth checking out to see if you can get into the game before you purchase the rest of the episodes.

Why?
A question I frequently asked myself. Why do I have to make these kinds of decisions. Why are the outcomes so unfair. Why, why, why...
The story really forces you to get personally involved. You have to learn all the characters, think ahead of what your actions may do and eventually decide the outcome of people's lives. And as the events spiral out of control, you can do nothing but sit and feel helpless. If you think you've discovered the solution, you are going to get a crippling shock.
Gameplay is really fun and I love how you can interact with almost anything. The camera can be a bit of a pain sometimes, but then again, it would make some aspects easy.
The characters are excellent. Each one has a decent backstory and, like everyone in life, is a bit damaged. Some more than others. I loved how I could unravel each character's personality and story amd how this game makes a animetd cluster of pixels seem so human. Well done on that, to the developers.
Visually the game wasn't breathtaking, but it luckily it also wasn't minecraft.
Ultimately, I really really enjoyed this game. I got to get involved in complex characters and see what consequences my actions had and how some reacted. Besides the feelings of being helpless, the moral of the story becomes all the obvious as you near the end: Life is Strange.

Unlike a lot of multiple choice games, you'll be glad to know that you will actually get to choose the underlying storyline's final outcome, as well as a series of minor and major choices along the way, which can make it easier or harder for you to reach the end point. Also, due to the huge impact some of these choices can make, it makes the game very replayable as the storyline doesn't feel monotone upon replay and branches off in several ways. It's also very easy to miss things so even going back the third time around, I have found new things. This game is hugely detailed, from Max's journal entries, to Chloe's reoccuring graffiti, and even being able to leave messages on boards for people to read can carry consequences. The graphics aren't hugely demanding yet beautiful and the music matches the atmosphere and character's personalities perfectly.
For the completionists out there,  there are all the optional photos to take. It is also nice to be able to compare world and friends stats on the choices.
Obviously if you're not a fan of story driven games you may be sceptical of the time travel premise. However it never feels forced or overally cliche, so as this game comes in episodes I recommend you at least try out the first one. If you do love this style of game go straight for the full pack, it takes so many unexpected turns and the characters are so lovable right from the start. I highly recommend it.

I had been tracking this game for a long time, but never gave it much attention. A friend of mine recommended it to me. I bought the entire season for $15, and boy do I regret not buying it since the get-go. For anyone that might be looking to buy this game, if you're a caffeine-driven, attention deficit person - you will not get through this game. Life is Strange is slow paced, and not in a bad way. It takes it time to develop character and narrative. However, once it hooks you, it takes you away from your life and into Arcadia Bay, following Max Caulfield. Without spoiling much of its story, it's a point 'n' click story, with cause and effect has the central mechanic of the game (like Telltale games).
Life is Strange is visually stunning, not because it has high quality textures, but because its art style is amazing and I'm pretty sure it's going to last a while until it gets dated (if ever). The story of this game is pretty good, but not flawless, especially regarding your choices. Some choices are not very impactful,  or are just dumb to pick because there was no follow-up to them. This game has two endings, depending on your choices but only one makes sense.  Regarding voice acting, most of them are pretty good but I have no point out that Chloe's actress, Ashly Burch, did an amazing job. All in all, to me the best part of this game is hands down the soundtrack. Original songs are fantastic and mix so well with the licensed ones.
I'd say Life is Strange is the 'Boyhood' of videogames. It's overall a sad game, where you are riding a rollercoaster of emotions called life.  9/10

So, in my early access review I complained a lot about how the "Career Mode" was incredibly tedious for this kind of game. Since then, the game has had some serious updates and has been officially released. Emphasis on "serious". I don't know if I hadn't played it for long enough, or if they had updated a few things, but for me it now has that anyone-can-do-it feel back. But enough of me referencing a review that is now gone, let me give you my final review for this game:
Kerbal Space Program is an RTS space sandbox/space program simulator set in another world far away from ours, yet similar in many ways. You play as a race of cute little green men called "Kerbals" (hence the name) that are in charge of a space program. It is your one and only true goal to manage this space program and to make it the best of the best. This requires researching new tech, building complex spacecraft, and choosing from an assortment of camaigns/strategies to increase your income in a specific field.
There are three main things that you must manage: reputation, money, and science. Your reputation determines how willingly people sign up to be a part of your program and how willingly people will offer you contracts. Your money is what you use to purchase parts and to upgrade different facilities. Finally, science is used to research the parts you will need to get to space and beyond. Another thing to note is that there are ores. As of now I do not have that much experience, and I have yet to see them. However, I assume they are used to buid things on the go and provide extra fuel for your long space journeys (the ladder I know is true).
This, however, is only true if you play career mode. There are a few other modes along with a custom one, where you can edit different options like money earned and cost of parts, to choose from. As I said earlier, there is a sandbox mode where you don't have to worry about money or reputation or science and you can build what you like. In this mode all facilities are upgraded to the max and all parts are already researched for you. This is if you just want to mess around with designs, or want to play without limitations. For those who like the idea of earning points to research parts but aren't a big fan of money and reputation holding them back, there is science mode. Science mode is similar to career mode, but without money and reputation. Think of it as a toned-down version of career mode. There is still something to work towards, but nothing is stopping you if you want to make a giant cruise missile out of some solid fuel boosters.
I could go on for paragraphs, but I think you get the point of the game.
TLDR Mark:
Pros:
Excellent progression system
Great graphics (for a game of this scale)
Astonishing physics and aerodynamics
Amazing soundtrack
Great modding support and community
Good for all Kinds of players
One of the few Early Access games that made it out of Early Access
Cons:
Can get tedious at times
Time consuming
Incredibly HARD and UNFORGIVING learning curve
Final Verdict: Kerbal space program is a great space exploration game that teaches people the lifelong lesson of why we use the phrase "It's not rocket science". Great for casuals, try-hards, and noobs alike. Overall I give it a 9/10. Nothing's better than the first time you get to the moon and realize you don't have enough fuel to get back.
