The game is good. Let me just get this off my chest :) It’s worth playing although I do not think it is 10 out of 10. And her is why.
The game is using a general concept and mechanic that is… well not the newest. It takes the classic concept used by Telltale Games and fortunately adds something new. The time rewind mechanic is actually cool and refreshing. Brings a lot of new possibilities into somewhat stagnant genre. This relatively simple mechanic simply adds value and fun to the game. And that’s basically it about mechanics. Otherwise it’s more or less what we know from last few years of episode split adventure games.
The story is also quite compelling and although being a 32 years old man from Poland makes it kind of hard to get into the shoes of an 18 years old American hipster teenager developers still managed to capture me into the story. It is interesting, intriguing and compelling. Up until a point in which developers started to try and explain the whole time travel mechanic stuff. Just then, close to the very end it starts to show holes and misconceptions. Some explanations for me personally felt rushed and not entirely thought thru.
The most disappointing thing in the game also made me realize the best thing about it. Disappointment? It was the ending. I felt like all what I played thru came to be irrelevant. The finale was just a binary choice that actually didn’t feel like taking into account any of the game decisions. Those just come off as storytelling devices. Moreover for like a half of the last episode you kinda had a feeling what that choice is going to be cause the build up to it was very obvious. But that’s also where comes the good part.
I think that if the ending♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥me off as lackluster and a bit cheap that means that I got invested in the characters and their story. So I feel like the game is more about build a relationship with the characters. The choice at the end is binary but it implicates consequence for the characters. And as felt emotionally invested in those consequences then I think this means that developers did what they intended. They have built my connection to those characters and, although simplified and this frustrating, the finale was what they intended it to be.

KSP is all about running a space agency and space exploration. You can design a spacecraft from a given set of parts, launch it, collect science and perform missions with it. It's set in a fictional solar system, with the main planet being Kerbin: a planet similar to Earth but populated by Kerbals. You must hire Kerbals for your missions. There are two game modes: Sandbox, where you do whatever you want and Career, where you start off with only a few parts and must perform science to unlock more parts. For a game in alpha, it is fun and amazing to play, with a wide array of things to do. One can only wonder what the final version will be like. It is a bit challenging though, as playing the game requires a basic knowledge of orbital mechanincs. The recent Asteroid Redirect Mission pack added new NASA-style parts to the game and asteroids, which can be brought to Kerbin orbit by ships equipped with a claw. The next update, according to the developers will add money to the game. If you ever feel the need for more parts, you can always download one of the many great mods available for this game. Note that with every new version the price increases, so if you don't buy it now you may end up paying more for it later on. 100% recomended.

A prime example of how an Early Access game should be handled. KSP is a strong title with a very simple but addicting premise: build a flying machine to explore the Kerbol system. A great game that becomes grandiose after installing some MODs!
There a few negative points, that in the end, are overwhelmingly surpassed by the positive aspects. The game is based on the Unity engine so... Squad, the developers, did their best but you should be aware that the game as frequent "hiccups" that completely halt everything for a split second. Also on the annoying side are the constant "memory leaks" that are exacerbated the more MODs you add. The game will eventually crash due to 32 bit memory limitation no matter what. Just restart and reload your save...
Read on for a description of the game mechanics:
I'll talk about the career mode which I think is the most interesting aspect of this game:
You start with some funds and a limited set of "parts" from which you can craft a basic rocket. From there, it all gets more complex and interesting. You can obtain more fundings to build bigger and better crafts by completing contracts. For example, in the beginning, a contract could ask you to reach 5000 meters in altitude. Similarly, to expand and research new or better parts, you need to do some scientific experiments. Contracts, most of the time, can grant you science points when completed or you can do your own experiments by, for example, going into orbit and analyzing a "GOO" container that you brought with you on the vessel. Taking surface samples, starting on your home planet of Kerbin, is another of the many ways in which you can obtain science points. As you complete more and more complex contracts, you gain reputation which allows you access to more advance and rewarding contracts and so on...
The games features a decent 3D engine that allows for close up and distant rendering of planets and moons. The Kerbol system features more than a dozen of those celestial bodies which can all be explored. From lift off to distant landing on an alien world, the rendering engine allows for a seamless 3D representation from anywhere in this star system.
Which bring us to orbital maneuvers and rocket science in general. The game learning curves is kind of slow and you will probably reach a point where you will need to "learn how it all works" by reading some online text on the KSP Wiki for example. But fear not, as complicated as rocket science can be, you do not need to have a profound mathematical understanding of what is going on to achieve great things in Kerbal Space Program; Just a basic understanding of orbital mechanics.
A very interesting aspect of KSP is the MOD community. A lot of creative and genuinely brilliant persons have created quite a bit of modifications for this game. From improved textures to new vessel parts to utility MODs like autopilot and navigation aids, you can and are in fact advised to take a look at what the different MODs can do to help you out and improve the gameplay experience. The sheer amount of dedication put forth by the different creators remind me of the community behind Minecraft...
After a while, and after building countless rockets and crafts, you will probably end up like me: I just can't stop thinking about KSP! What will my next craft be? A vertical takeoff plane to explore planet Kerbin? What about a simple three stages rocket to send a satellite into orbit? No wait, a huge craft with multiple stages and a detachable landing module to reach planet Duna!
From building to flying to crashing this game offers it all in a sweet comics inspired package!

Where do I even begin to describe this game.  I suppose the obvious words come to mind:  Fun... Challenging... and Very Very Unique.
I say Unique, because I mainly play space Sims and D&D type games; this game is more like the Sims in the since you're not battling some evil force, but more like living day to day, but as a Rocket Sciencetist.  But more than the Sims, it's almost a learning tool; at a very low level... but still - I accidently learned a fews things today - Whoops.
The characters in the game are fun by themselves.  Comically done, but with a hint of Animated Believeablity; in short, a Whimsical Race of beings who oddly remind you of simplier times.
But lets talk about game play.  I won't lie... this game has a serious learning curve; at least it did for me (I'm sure there are instructions somewhere; but I'd rather just Push and Play).  I've only got a few hours of game play in, but I'm still learning.  However, that is much of the fun of the game (Not so much of "How to Play the Game", but more about How to do Well in Playing the Game".  Imagine NASA when they first put together a handful of people, and said, "Let's explore Space."  Well, you have to figure there were a lot of trial and errors as they learned the Do's and Don'ts of space travel.  Well, I'm beginning to see what they went through.  After several failed attempts to leave the Stratosphere (and a few law suits); I finally built a rocket that didn't just fall over before take off.... do a 180 and then a Header into the ground... or my favorite - Engage the 4th Stage Rocket before the 2nd and 3rd Stage Rockets... and off into the Wild Blue Yonder I went.  Actually, I didn't quite make it to Orbit, but I did make a safe landing (Woot), and learned a little more, and am now a little closer to my goal; Which for the record I have set for myself; the game, even in its 'somewhat' campaign mode, doesn't force you to go to one place or another; it's not quite sandbox (which it does offer), but not mission based either, which I'm not a fan of; You just decided what your goal is going to be... and good luck.
The point (which I'm slying avoiding is) this game's mechanics is the true fun of it.  Attempting to learn, figure out and understand the physics of Avaiation and Space Travel.  I wouldn't say it will make a physics expert out of you, but it will definitely give you a little understand of it.  And with each failure, you'll find yourself a little more knowledgable about what it takes to leave our atmosphere.
But lastly, and most importantly... let's not forget that this is a GAME!!!  I'm confident it will provide me Hours of Challenging Fun.  I've already spent the last few hours just trying to leave orbit.. but next goal (WHEN I get out of orbit - lol) is to reach the moon.. and from there, it seems there are a decent handful of places to explore there after (to be completely honest, it doesn't seem like there are 'LOT' of places (maybe 10 or so), but considering what it will take to actually get to one, makes up for any Possible lack of places to explore) (NOTE: I use the term 'Lack of Places' loosely, I'm still trying to fully understand the Tracking and Map few of the system).  And if that's not enough, from what I've ready prior to purchasing this game, it is (or maybe, will be) Workshop enabled; which means once the fun dies down... the modders will re-light the fires.  I judge games on several factors... but for me, one of the most important factors is how many hours will I get out of a game... Enjoyably.  I like to get my money's worth... and about 10 other people money's worth as well.  This game promises to do such, IMHO!!!
So yes... I most definitely would Recommed this game.  Oh... and as to Stability... another very important factor; after (again) only a few hours of game play, I found now problems running everything on high... Good Frame Rate, no lag, no crashes (well, except a few of the rockets I built - LOL), and no problems (Game Play wise).
Good Luck... hope you enjoy this as much as I am!!!
EDIT:  P.S. After posting the review I decided to check how many hours I actually had; and at the time of this posting it was 7 hours; so I can add ADDICTIVE to words I would use to describe this game :).

A prime example of how an Early Access game should be handled. KSP is a strong title with a very simple but addicting premise: build a flying machine to explore the Kerbol system. A great game that becomes grandiose after installing some MODs!
There a few negative points, that in the end, are overwhelmingly surpassed by the positive aspects. The game is based on the Unity engine so... Squad, the developers, did their best but you should be aware that the game as frequent "hiccups" that completely halt everything for a split second. Also on the annoying side are the constant "memory leaks" that are exacerbated the more MODs you add. The game will eventually crash due to 32 bit memory limitation no matter what. Just restart and reload your save...
Read on for a description of the game mechanics:
I'll talk about the career mode which I think is the most interesting aspect of this game:
You start with some funds and a limited set of "parts" from which you can craft a basic rocket. From there, it all gets more complex and interesting. You can obtain more fundings to build bigger and better crafts by completing contracts. For example, in the beginning, a contract could ask you to reach 5000 meters in altitude. Similarly, to expand and research new or better parts, you need to do some scientific experiments. Contracts, most of the time, can grant you science points when completed or you can do your own experiments by, for example, going into orbit and analyzing a "GOO" container that you brought with you on the vessel. Taking surface samples, starting on your home planet of Kerbin, is another of the many ways in which you can obtain science points. As you complete more and more complex contracts, you gain reputation which allows you access to more advance and rewarding contracts and so on...
The games features a decent 3D engine that allows for close up and distant rendering of planets and moons. The Kerbol system features more than a dozen of those celestial bodies which can all be explored. From lift off to distant landing on an alien world, the rendering engine allows for a seamless 3D representation from anywhere in this star system.
Which bring us to orbital maneuvers and rocket science in general. The game learning curves is kind of slow and you will probably reach a point where you will need to "learn how it all works" by reading some online text on the KSP Wiki for example. But fear not, as complicated as rocket science can be, you do not need to have a profound mathematical understanding of what is going on to achieve great things in Kerbal Space Program; Just a basic understanding of orbital mechanics.
A very interesting aspect of KSP is the MOD community. A lot of creative and genuinely brilliant persons have created quite a bit of modifications for this game. From improved textures to new vessel parts to utility MODs like autopilot and navigation aids, you can and are in fact advised to take a look at what the different MODs can do to help you out and improve the gameplay experience. The sheer amount of dedication put forth by the different creators remind me of the community behind Minecraft...
After a while, and after building countless rockets and crafts, you will probably end up like me: I just can't stop thinking about KSP! What will my next craft be? A vertical takeoff plane to explore planet Kerbin? What about a simple three stages rocket to send a satellite into orbit? No wait, a huge craft with multiple stages and a detachable landing module to reach planet Duna!
From building to flying to crashing this game offers it all in a sweet comics inspired package!

To put this simply, I truly enjoyed this game and consider it a work of art. I have a lot of details to share, but if you just want to get the gist of my opinion; I would highly recommend this game.
The story is well pieced together, and uses great design to make itself more enjoyable and immersive. The main concept is amazing, and its great to see.
Something I really liked about the game however, is the points in which you are given time to sit and listen to your character’s thoughts. I often found myself sitting longer than the duration of the monolog. It is a very effective way of breaking up the action, and giving you time to let your actions sink in.
If you pay good enough attention, you can catch some really well placed foreshadowing, which is revealed around the end of the game in the last episode. I really appreciate the detail that went into writing the story, and outcomes.
I think that the best way to experience the game is to play through the game in one session. I was able to do this, and I was often so emerged into the world that I had to remind myself to take breaks, It is important to take breaks during this game, because it was exactly 16 hours that I played through, and sitting that long is unhealthy. I suggest taking a break or two every episode and in between episodes (or at the very least just between episodes).

Life is Strange is a sci-fi mystery that becomes more and more intense and insane as the story progresses.
Heavy Rain is one of my all-time favorite games and this game is a lot like it in the way that it is an interactive movie and events can be altered by the player. In Life is Strange, everything you choose to do or choose not to do has consequences. Even all the bits of information you collect when walking around examining things is important.
I love the feel of the game, the music. The beginning is a bit slow, but the character building is well done. This game is also an emotional roller coaster. The characters are developed in a way that makes you feel as though they are real people who's lives you become invested in.
It does have some replay value, as you can make different choices and two different game endings. There are also photos that you can take throughout the game (they're listed in Max's journal) and this requires replaying in order to find all the photo spots.
This game is amazing and well worth the $25 I spent on it - 10/10.

*I believe I got this game years ago on my crummy 50$ pc when Garry's Mod was on sale for $1.99 (or something like that) *
For a game that came out over a decade ago its amazing that it is talked about even more now than ever - (it's the reason I got a PC anyway)
There are some awesome things and there are some bad things about Garry's Mod, so far I have put in around 1,600 hours over 4 years (2 months nonstop) and one thing that annoys me to no end is "missing textures," the purple and black checkerboard textures that inhabit garry's mod - It's like a sidequest in a game that only leads to more side quests. (AVGN Reference)
1st you have to own garrys mod, and next you need to own CSS (counter strike source) which IS a necessity because most addons require it. Next, you will find that not only do most community addons require CSS, but some use HLF2 EP2 or some other obscure game like DoD as a source of textures or mechanics.
Something else that gets on my nerves is just how much Garry's Mod requires trial and error, you are going to be figuring out what addons work with what and constantly checking your game cache.
But even after all the annoying texture solving, the game IS fantastic and is the best example of a sandbox game today, there is 100% nothing else like it on steam, and everyone should own a copy.
SOME PROS:
Any game that utilizes the steam workshop is going to have a very long shelf life, such as Gmod
No money grubbing DLC
Cheap
Single Player and Multiplayer
No end goal, forcing you to create the challenges for yourself
Half building/constructing game, half "Kill everyone" game
(choose to build a mansion with the supplied props, or spawn combine and drop a nuke on them)
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SOME CONS:
No easy way to create private servers for you and your friends [Not LAN] there is no "create private server" option (you have to use hamachi)
Textures & addon debugging
Wait timers for entering a server for the first time can be WAY to long

The story (through chapters 1-4) is definitely good, and I liked that my choices appeared to matter throughout those chapters.  But as many others said, in the end there is only one choice you have to make, and it pretty much erases every other decision you made in the game.   I had originally thought I would replay the game to make some different choices, but after playing the last chapter I've decided against it.
Physics!
Countless hours of pure fun!

Bad things:
Maybe I am too old and no longer understand how teenagers work, but I found the constant drama a little irritating. It gets better after a while though.
Also, I didn't find the game to be such an emotional rollercoaster as many reviews have said. But that may just be me being generally uninterested in the nuances of human relationships. I'm more of a hard SF guy.
Good things:
A lot of good things, actually. Maybe the most detailed and engaging story ever told by a game. Worth it just for that.
There are some really deep underlying ideas and metaphors and I'm not sure I have found all of them. Makes one think.
Beautiful visuals and superb voice acting, and the perfect soundtrack. Nothing feels rushed, the puzzles do not break immersion and exploring the game world always feel rewarding, never like a chore.
Some parts of the story I found deeply touching.
In summary: Buy it. It's worth it for the story alone.

If you ever get bored of the game then you can visit the space port website where you can download hundreds of modifications to the game, including physics changing ones!

I just finished the game a few minutes ago and had to leave a review while it was still fresh in my mind.
It has been years since a game has affected me on such an emotional level. This game pulls you into the story and makes you love the characters and believe in the relationships between them. It's a game that rewards you for talking to everyone and exploring everything. The choices you make matter. Most importantly, there are many choices that don't have a clear good or bad answer, and you have to decide for yourself what you'd rather live with.
The dialogue between the characters and the way you can affect what they do later on has to be my favorite part of the game. Being nice to someone can literally save their life in later scenes. Also, the relationship between the two main characters is so incredibly real and amazing to watch.
There are still tears in my eyes afterward. I would highly recommend this to anyone who likes story-rich, choice-based games that are filled with emotion.

The Butterfly Effect Game as told by Telltale Games.
SIMILAR GAMES: Any game by Telltale Games (The Walking Dead, Game of Thrones, Wolf Among Us)
SIMILAR MOVIES: The Butterfly Effect
MEET MAX. Mad Max. Spider Max. Super Max. Maximum Overdrive (you get a lot of those during the game so brace yourselves). She's just your normal, respected loner teenage girl going through the most difficult journey in her life - high school. When you come across your childhood bestie for the first time in 5 years, Max discoveries she has an ability to time travel. Instead of traveling back through time to experience all of life's mysteries or help people find a cure for cancer, she will do the unthinkable - use her powers to overcome high school drama and pre pubescent angst. Come across all those personas that use to make high school miserable for us - the jock deuche, the spoiled brat, the rich beeach, the trendy hipster, the blazed out junkie, the passive aggressive nerd, and a bunch of others you don't really remember because they are purely supportive characters. Reunited with her best friend and her new abilities to rip through time, Max will go from ZERO to HERO to ZERO again back to HERO and this goes on for a while because much like most women, she's indecisive and doesn't know what to do with her powers.... even if you do and tell her what to do.
That's the basic gist of it. Folks, I want to remind you that this is an INTERACTIVE MOVIE. This is not a game. This is one of those "WALKING SIMULATORS." There is a very, very, very small amount of gameplay. You chat up one person and then you chat up another and this is 98% of the "game." You use your time traveling abilities to figure out what you think is the best response to their questions and then you move on. And you keep doing this over and over and over again. There are 5 "episodes" to this game (oh the irony to having episodes in a video game). Episode 1 is high school. 2 to 5 you start to do other interesting stuff such as figure out what happened to a missing girl. It takes off by the end of episode 2. The longer you use your powers, the more messed up crap that happens in nature around you. Your ultimate goal is to find out what happened to the missing chick and to save the town from the side effects of your powers. If you don't think that sounds like fun, it won't be. If you are looking for a fun GAME, look elsewhere. This is not a game. This is a movie and it's as enjoyable as the Butterfly Effect (which I loved). In fact, it's so freakishly similar, it could be a damn sequel to it.
Overall, I enjoyed it but it's not easy to get into. Be prepared to listen for around 14 or so hours while having 1 hour of real gameplay. No multiplayer. No coop. No leaderboards. Great soundtrack though. FINAL SCORE: 7.5/10. Can't go wrong for $3. Recommended ONLY if you like interactive movies. NOT recommended if you are looking for an actual GAME.

Edit: Sorry for the wall of text, I just finished the game when I wrote this and I had a lot to say about it.
Edit 2: Also sorry if it is a little hard to follow, as it was around midnight when I wrote this and was very tired.
Review:
So by the time I have written this review, I have just finished the game.
When I purchased this game, I knew little to nothing about it, only that it was suppose to be pretty good.  I can honestly say that it shattered my expectations (in a great way).  So let's me dive into the aspects:
Gameplay:
It is very smooth.  Very easy to learn controls.  If you have played TellTale's The Walking Dead, I assume the controls are very similar (played it on a mobile device, have seen gameplay on pc/console.  Just making an assumption, so please do not quote me on that).  There were a few occational framerate issues, but nothing that was game-breaking or lasting for an entire ingame conversation.  The most was like at most half a second.
Art style:
Right as the title menue appears, you can already tell this will be a beautiful game.  Right after I had started the game, it was visually gorgeous.  Nothing else to really say
Story:
This here is where the game truely shines.  Sadly, anything I could say to describe the story would spoil the game, and it is something that you really need to experience yourself.  Like I had said previously, I had heard great things about this game, and it had shattered my expectations.  This is mainly because of the story.  What I can say about it is that its characters are highly relatable, the plot keeps you engaged up until the very end, and, most definitely, it is very emotional.  Many reviews say that this game will make you cry, and they are not lying, as I have through multiple parts of the game.  That truely shows how amazing this game is.  If the characters and the story can connect with you on that much of an emotional level, and many people who have written reviews for this have used the words "emotional rollercoaster," then it is a game that one shoud definitely check out.  Not only that, but it is suspenseful.  At the end of every episode, I found myself wanting more, to find out what will happen next, and I personally enjoyed it more because of that.
To sum up:
Square Enix has truely created a gem.  If anyone reading this has a chance, please check out this game.  Besides the very few framerate issues (like less than .000001% for me at least), the gameplay is smooth, the artstyle is beautiful, and the story is gripping and will hold onto you throughout the very end.  It may be an "emotional rollercoaster," but it is one that I can say is worth riding.
I rate this game 10/10.
Edit 2 continued:  I can give the basic plot: You play as a High School Senior at Blackwell High School, Max Caulfield.  She discovers that she has the power of DirecTV (the power to turn back time), and uses it with the help of her friend to solve the misterious disapperance of a local girl who went to the same school.  It does deal with a few parts of the HS drama stuffs, one of which is bullying.  Also, in this game, your choices do matter as to how the story will progress for you.  Depending on your choices, certain caracters can have different opinions of you, certain actions will have different outcomes, and certain characters can live or die.  It's definitely one of the best games I personally have ever played and I would recommend you to check it out.  My rating stays the same at a 10/10, would definitely cry again.

I really wanted to like this game. I kept reading the wonderful reviews and was ready to give it a try. But even by just the first episode completed, I can't stand this game.
The good:
The detail of content in the game and the visuals are great. And the rewind concept including into the storyline is great especially for choose-your-adventure type games.
The bad:
So, whether or not you believe in climate change, this game goes over the top. I realize nearly every single movie or story has to have some mention to climate change in todays culture in order to push the line and be considered for quality, but this game was ridiculously over the top on it. In just the first episode alone (which takes about an hour of play), there was at least a half dozen mentions of climate change. An hour, and at least six mentions of it, that's once every ten minutes... And not even any valid mentions either, but the really idiotic ("it's been so hot lately, thanks climate change!") crap, or "It's snowing?!?!? CLIMATE CHANGE!". Even supporters of climate change know how idiotic this is and actually harms the argument.
Then, the hatred of the rich. More than climate change, the game pushes the full blown outright hatred of the rich, anyone rich, anyone related to anyone rich, anyone that has something nicer that the protagonist, etc. The soppy protagonist goes around acting as if she understands how awful stereotypes are, and then commits all of them at every turn. To call this a "video game" just wouldn't give it justice. What makes life is strange different than any other game is that its main characters are round and deep. Each one is complex in their own way. Even the stereotypical mean girl has her own quirks. The characters naturally drive the story and are often easy to relate with. The characters in this story struggle with very real problems in the world today and the player truly feels the emotion inherent in the situations. This game, or rather story, critiques the traditional modern day American high school experience. Including the high school hierarchy of popularity, and as well as new modern day phenomenons teens today face including sexting, viral videos, and the effect of social media. Not only that, there are also topics of depression, bullying, violence, and their effect on teens and their emotional and mental health. The player will find themselves comfronted with these situations and the emotion that this game captures is truly moving. The characters also feel like real human beings and act naturally, which is what I think makes this story interesting and sometimes heartbreaking. The player feels a connection to the main characters and their humanity which is why every decision seems meaningful and the player truly wants things to turn out fine. When the player makes a decision, they are faced with the consequences and sometimes, when a bad decision is made, it can be difficult for the player to live with that decision. The opposite is true when the player succeeds, there truly is a feeling of joy when a character thanks you or what they have to say. When something terrible happens, the player feels devastated. Life is strange is captivating and is  true masterpiece from dontnod entertainment and what I consider a true modern day work of art. I think almost anyone can relate to some of the themes of this game which is why I would recommend it because I think everyone will find something meaningful to take away from this game and the story truly is riveting. Life is strange is truly a modern day masterpiece, and no words can describe it.

Of all the games I’ve purchased on Steam during the Steam Summer Sale, I have to say Life is Strange, produced by Dontnod Entertainment and Square Enix, is by far my favorite purchase. I got it on a whim because it included the tag “time travel” and was less than ten dollars in total, and I am but a simple girl who loves a good time travel narrative. I didn’t know what to expect from this game, but in all honestly I didn’t expect much.
Instead, I’ve stayed up way too late the past two days doing nothing but play this game.
I actually hesitate to label this a “game” because it doesn’t feel like any game I’ve played before. I’d call it more like a visual novel or choose your own adventure book with a little bit of puzzle mixed in. The story in it is what really sells the game, as well as the enjoyable characters.
If I had to sum up the game, I would say this: teenage girl discovers both superpowers and lesbianism. She decides to explore both. She thinks she’s living in either a superhero origin story or a Nancy Drew novel, but discovers 3/4ths of the way through that she’s actually in a horror movie.
The game isn’t without it’s flaws: there were several times when I yelled at the screen that “YOU HAVE A SMART PHONE, WHY WON’T YOU USE IT”. There’s a twist that occurs in episode three that I found interesting at first, but simply dragged on for too long without enough impact on the plot (it should have been shortened or cut OR explored with more depth--at the moment it seems it was used primarily for shock value and then too much time was spent there for it not to be all that relevant.) And the ending--while interesting--is lackluster and unfulfilling.
PLEASE NOTE that there should be some sort of trigger warning for parts of the game. Like, LOTS of trigger warnings. So much so that I--someone who is fairly privileged and has nerves of steel--was disturbed with parts of the game if only due to the realism of the scenario. I won’t post what happens here for spoilers, but if you are wondering for yourself and want to know if it might trigger you, ask and I’ll tell you.
Despite this, I still highly recommend the game to anyone who loves story-based games or seeing games where their choices matter. Like I said, I’ve spent the past two days playing it non-stop--which is high praise from me indeed.

This isn't so much a game as it is an adventure. You can complete it in about 10-15 hours, depending on how you play.
It's primarily a choice based game, but you control Max, and can move around and interact with side characters.
The characters you mainly interact with will feel like your friends, like they're real. When I finished this game I felt empty inside. Mostly because it was such a good story, but also because I don't think I'll ever find something like this again.
The game is very visceral, and it deals with a lot of things that may make you uncomfortable, but don't let that steer you away, it's all part of the story; a very good one, I can't stress this enough.
Dontnod crafted a story that I haven't been able to stop thinking about for several months, and every once in a while I go back and play it just to reminisce.
The soundtrack is phenomenal. It adds so much feeling to the story, and it really transports you to the location the game is set in.
It's an easy 10/10.
If you haven't tried it yet, and you're on the fence about this game, just buy it. It's a steal at $10. The first episode is even free, so there's no excuse.

I have finished this game many times on both the PC and Xbox One and I have to say it is one of my favorite games specifically because of the storyline and the amount of objects you can interact with. I discovered this game on the Steam Store about a year ago and purchased it due to it having a very low price of five USD for all five episodes. But before making an investment in the game, I had to check the system requirements because I use a Laptop that uses an Intel Core i5 processor (Not that very capable for gaming) and discovered that this game runs pretty well on average settings. This game also runs on Unreal Engine so the quality is not over the top AAA quality but it is satisfying if you are interested in the story rather than focusing on the graphics and lip syncing.
Without revealing any spoilers, "Life is Strange" takes place in a fictional world taking place in the town of Arcadia Bay, Oregon. Here our main protagonist, Maxine Caulfield. is enrolled at an art school known as Blackwell Academy. Here she mainly focuses on taking photograpghy classes under the instructor, Mark Jefferson, until discovering that she has the ability to rewind time shortly after events take place. She eventually saves a girl's life using this ability and from that point . tries to discover the secrets of the town while trying to find a missing person named, Rachel Amber.
The story is very touching especially near the end and what makes this game interesting is the fact that certain actions have effect on the future of the story. For instance, you have the oppritunity to report a student for having a gun in the school. Will you report him and risk getting bullied? Or will you keep quiet? Depending on what you choose, the story in the future will be affected by it. But since Max has the oppritunity to rewind time, you can change your answer or action right after you make it if you do not like the immidiate outcome. I highly recommend this game to anyone.

The first time you pick up Kerbal Space Program, you might find it a little intimidating. This is normal. KSP is a robust rocketry simulator that does not suffer fools. However, even the failures are highly entertaining and this game does not stop being fun.
The first rocket you build may get a few kilometers up. The second, a little higher. You may reach space on a sub orbital trajectory after that, but soon, you will achieve stable orbit. It'll be then that you take a look beyond the shores of Kerbin, the Kerbal homeworld, and see the challenges ahead of you. The Mun, Duna, Eve and even the mighty Jool test your resolve.
I have been playing Kerbal for a long time now, since one of the early versions where you had the choice of a couple engines and a very twitchy stabilization system. Now you can research Mun rocks, build space stations and send probes all over the Kerbolar system.
For replayability, challenge and reward and the sheer amount of fun you have throwing Kerbals around at enormous velocities, I consider KSP to be a contender for the greatest game of all time.

So let me say right off the bat, this game will not be for everyone, But you more than likely know before you read this review if the game is even close to up your alley.  In career mode, It takes a patience, common sense. There is alot of trial and error. I had seen alot of the reviews and decided that I was going to not visit any guides or wikis, Which made the game much more gratifying knowing I figured it out on my own.  After nearly 100 hours into the game, im getting ready to restart career and impose a hardcore mode on myself.  As stated on the main page of the game, this is early access, therefore still alot missing from the game, you almost have to make your own fun out of it ATM. But even with features still missing, the game is alot of fun, I always consider a game worth the money if I get a dollar a hour out of it, this game far surpasses that, even off sale.
The physics of the game are very solid and very unforgiving, just like it should be. The amount of stuff  you can do is only limited by your imagination.  From orbiting a planet, to a complete Space Station around the games version of Mars.
I must say too that I am a bit worried that the updates have been so slow to come out, I got the game a few days before the asteroid missions and the sale (doh).  Come to find out that was the first update in something like 3 months.  That being said, I have also seen in rviews that the modding community is awesome, so that may make up for the lack of updates in a small way.  Becuase of my self imposed blackout on anything that could be a spoiler, i have not looked into the mods myself.  But after I get tired of my hardcore mode, thats my next stop.
Any questions, feel free to ask in the comments section.
Edit: I finally had to look up how to transfer fuel.  Spent 3 hours clicking on a docked craft trying to figure it out. :/

Of course this is still early access, but is already showing great potential and has tons of stuff to do. What stuff you may ask? Launching little green men into space then realizing once in orbit that you cannot get him back so he must stay up there for years till a rescue can happen. Maybe rockets are more your thing, no worries, will be plenty of failed rockets exploding, summersaulting through the sky and of course the nice feeling of getting your first ship into space.....and maybe back to Earth. There is already tons of things to do in game between sandbox mode or career mode to keep you busy and constantly busy and even if that isn`t enough there are endless amounts of mods to add some more crazy to your space program. So in sort, this is the perfect game for you astronomers, casual game players, and well.....everyone! Just remember when having all that chaotic fun or maybe a success or two you will be learning meaningful things...in a game!

, and I've run without problems with 20 mods! Most sandbox games (Other than Minecraft, of course) cannot surpass this game's community content. The most astonishing fact about this, though, is that it is still in ALPHA. Alpha, and it has very few bugs. Alpha, and it is one of my favorite games. Alpha, and having streamlined modding. I rarely gush about anything, but Life Is Strange is phenomenal. An absolute triumph of interactive storytelling. It is not only the single best adventure game I have ever played (and I've played
of adventure games), but one of the best games of any genre ever. Ten out of ten; five stars; the highest possible score on any given metric - this game has earned it.
In 5 episodes it traverses so much thematic ground, surveys a rich emotional landscape, confronts ideas and plot developments that could so easily have been gauche were they not handled with such a deft touch. There are devastatingly emotional moments, quirky nods to Twin Peaks, John Hughes style teenage drama, and sequences that would not be out of place in a Silent Hill game. And it all flows perfectly. There is no deus ex machina. The many varying strands and styles of the narrative could so easily have turned into a garbled mess (e.g. any Quantic Dream game) and yet it all culminates in a truly epic crescendo of a finale that resolves everything, while, in true Lynchian style, actually explaining very little in full.
At its core, the story is about the power of friendship in the face of true evil. I came to care for these characters like few others, and I'm not ashamed to say that the unexpected narrative turns made me cry on more than one occasion. This is a feat that no other game has ever achieved.
The standard of its presentation is second to none. There is astonishing attention to detail in each and every one of its environments that make them feel truly lived-in and authentic. Beyond that, the soundtrack is superb with each song complementing the scene in which it appears perfectly, and the shot composition is equal to any well-made film.
Life Is Strange doesn't forget that it is also a game, and to that end provides a sort of 'Where's Wally' task whereby the in-game journal provides you with vague sketches of scenery you are meant to look out for in each episode, and subsequently photograph. It is a completely optional, unobtrusive task, that has no impact on the way the story develops, but I was glad it was there because it mechanically reinforces the narrative element of Max's abiding passion for photography.
Everything about Life Is Strange is well considered and perfectly executed. After the mediocre Remember Me, this is exactly what DONTNOD needed to establish their name as a quality development studio. I can't wait to see what they come up with next.

I rarely gush about anything, but Life Is Strange is phenomenal. An absolute triumph of interactive storytelling. It is not only the single best adventure game I have ever played (and I've played
of adventure games), but one of the best games of any genre ever. Ten out of ten; five stars; the highest possible score on any given metric - this game has earned it.
In 5 episodes it traverses so much thematic ground, surveys a rich emotional landscape, confronts ideas and plot developments that could so easily have been gauche were they not handled with such a deft touch. There are devastatingly emotional moments, quirky nods to Twin Peaks, John Hughes style teenage drama, and sequences that would not be out of place in a Silent Hill game. And it all flows perfectly. There is no deus ex machina. The many varying strands and styles of the narrative could so easily have turned into a garbled mess (e.g. any Quantic Dream game) and yet it all culminates in a truly epic crescendo of a finale that resolves everything, while, in true Lynchian style, actually explaining very little in full.
At its core, the story is about the power of friendship in the face of true evil. I came to care for these characters like few others, and I'm not ashamed to say that the unexpected narrative turns made me cry on more than one occasion. This is a feat that no other game has ever achieved.
The standard of its presentation is second to none. There is astonishing attention to detail in each and every one of its environments that make them feel truly lived-in and authentic. Beyond that, the soundtrack is superb with each song complementing the scene in which it appears perfectly, and the shot composition is equal to any well-made film.
Life Is Strange doesn't forget that it is also a game, and to that end provides a sort of 'Where's Wally' task whereby the in-game journal provides you with vague sketches of scenery you are meant to look out for in each episode, and subsequently photograph. It is a completely optional, unobtrusive task, that has no impact on the way the story develops, but I was glad it was there because it mechanically reinforces the narrative element of Max's abiding passion for photography.
Everything about Life Is Strange is well considered and perfectly executed. After the mediocre Remember Me, this is exactly what DONTNOD needed to establish their name as a quality development studio. I can't wait to see what they come up with next.

You accomplish feats your way, and damn it feels good to get something right. It even feels good to get something wrong and watch it all explode in the sky. There is no quick one-click warp to get to a planet; you need to design a ship with the capabilities you need to get it there, and then get it there!
Want to build starships, travel to other planets, and learn about orbits and spaceflight while doing it? Get Kerbal Space Program; the price is more than fair considering the powerful simulator and game you are buying. This game is worth a full $60. It's truly something unique, and you're missing out if you haven't played it.

Oh, this game.  Where do I begin?
Okay, let's start with the fact that this game is still under development, so while the game is awesome as it is, it can only get better from here.
I remember when I bought Kerbal Space Program.  I had just seen a playthrough of it on Markiplier's YouTube channel back when he was under 600K subs.  This game looked so dang fun that I just couldn't not pick it up and play it.
That was before I bought the game.......
I got sucked into this game so much that for the first weeks, I couldn't set it down.  While on YouTube, most people usually put a ship on the Mun (The moon of Kerbin, the home planet of the Kerbals for which the game was named.  Yeah, those little green guys are called Kerbals) and then call it good and never really move on.  There is so much more to this game.  So let's begin with its gameplay
GAMEPLAY:
I'm going to say this right off the bat, this is not a Scribblenauts-style draw a cute little rocket ship and then it blasts off into space.  No, in Kerbal Space Program, you better have a space worthy, stable, powerful spacecraft, or you will crash and burn quick.  Structural integrity, engine heat, weight and thrust distribution all play into how successful your spacecraft will be.  Another major point is that, realistically and in KSP, Spaceships don't just go through hyperspace or go in any sort of straight line to other places.  You have to do this yourself.  This may sound complicated, but the next point is the learning curve.
LEARNING CURVE:
While the above may sound strikingly complex, it really isn't.  The tutorials for this game are fantastic, and if they aren't enough, there are plenty of beginner videos out there (The best are by Scott Manley on YouTube, whose sexy scottish voice leads you through the ins and outs of building a space-worthy ship).  From starting with a cockpit, parachute, and a solid rocket booster, to making twenty stage rocket ships to blast off to the furthest reaches of the solar system, this game is meant to be taken very slowly, so be patient and the rewards will come to you.  Not to mention the maneuver node system is the most useful thing on the planet.
STORY:
Who needs a story when little green men jump around 30 feet on the moon?  I think there's no need for such a thing.
CONCLUSION:
This game is an absolute necessity to complete any gamer's library.  It really is the only game of its kind, and no one should be afraid to pick this game up and give it a try.  You will fail, a lot.  I know I did.  But be patient, take the game slowly, and eventually you'll be landing on Eve without even trying.
This game is absolutely worth the price it has, even in development.  Go and buy it.  Why are you reading this?  I have no idea what you're doing here, you should be playing this game.

The question that everyone asks when they are about to buy a game is "Is it good" Asking if Kerbal Space Program is a good game is like asking your high school chemistry teacher if throwing a bunch of random chemicals into a bin is a smart idea. Yes, the teacher is probably going to say no, but hey it was worth the shot. And that summarizes what Kerbal Space Program is. You try something and it ether works, or it fails in an spectacular way. Either way you learn ways not to fail so you can continue on your quest for all the science you can get. So if you like the trial and error style of games then yes, this game is good. If you don't like that kind of stuff, you can always find enjoyment in mindlessly launching helpless Kerbals into space (or at least trying) and if you like that, congratulations you sociopath, the game is still fun. If it still does not interest you, there are thousands of other games out there that you would probably like.  My point is Kerbal Space Program is fun, it’s a good game. But you need to like the style and time needed to get the best out of this game. When I first got this game, I decided to try to go to Jool (The game's equivalent to Jupiter) and I ended up getting five feet from the launch pad before my boosters tore of my rocket and went flying into its cockpit. In spite, i then put down the game and did not touch it for a few months.  But that’s the fun of the game. Trial and Error. That is why I love this game, and will continue to play it years and years. And if you are interested in things like this, go ahead don't wait, get the game right now!

Oh, this game.  Where do I begin?
Okay, let's start with the fact that this game is still under development, so while the game is awesome as it is, it can only get better from here.
I remember when I bought Kerbal Space Program.  I had just seen a playthrough of it on Markiplier's YouTube channel back when he was under 600K subs.  This game looked so dang fun that I just couldn't not pick it up and play it.
That was before I bought the game.......
I got sucked into this game so much that for the first weeks, I couldn't set it down.  While on YouTube, most people usually put a ship on the Mun (The moon of Kerbin, the home planet of the Kerbals for which the game was named.  Yeah, those little green guys are called Kerbals) and then call it good and never really move on.  There is so much more to this game.  So let's begin with its gameplay
GAMEPLAY:
I'm going to say this right off the bat, this is not a Scribblenauts-style draw a cute little rocket ship and then it blasts off into space.  No, in Kerbal Space Program, you better have a space worthy, stable, powerful spacecraft, or you will crash and burn quick.  Structural integrity, engine heat, weight and thrust distribution all play into how successful your spacecraft will be.  Another major point is that, realistically and in KSP, Spaceships don't just go through hyperspace or go in any sort of straight line to other places.  You have to do this yourself.  This may sound complicated, but the next point is the learning curve.
LEARNING CURVE:
While the above may sound strikingly complex, it really isn't.  The tutorials for this game are fantastic, and if they aren't enough, there are plenty of beginner videos out there (The best are by Scott Manley on YouTube, whose sexy scottish voice leads you through the ins and outs of building a space-worthy ship).  From starting with a cockpit, parachute, and a solid rocket booster, to making twenty stage rocket ships to blast off to the furthest reaches of the solar system, this game is meant to be taken very slowly, so be patient and the rewards will come to you.  Not to mention the maneuver node system is the most useful thing on the planet.
STORY:
Who needs a story when little green men jump around 30 feet on the moon?  I think there's no need for such a thing.
CONCLUSION:
This game is an absolute necessity to complete any gamer's library.  It really is the only game of its kind, and no one should be afraid to pick this game up and give it a try.  You will fail, a lot.  I know I did.  But be patient, take the game slowly, and eventually you'll be landing on Eve without even trying.
This game is absolutely worth the price it has, even in development.  Go and buy it.  Why are you reading this?  I have no idea what you're doing here, you should be playing this game.

I played through this 3 times. Once as my first playthrough. Another with my girlfriend. And finally with special keybindings that let me clip in and out of areas. I want to talk about all 3.
1st playthrough:
This is such an emotional game. It's so easy to get attached to Max and Chloe. I just can't describe how sucked in to this story I got. It's a feeling I haven't had from a game in years. I wanted to be Max's best friend and I wanted Chloe to just be happy. Seriously, if you haven't already, play this game. And once you get to the end, don't worry, there have already been talks of a Life Is Strange Season 2.
2nd playthrough:
Watching my girlfriend play this game I would often go "Oh Sh** I didn't even realize that"! to which she would look at me  in confusion and I realized how little you think the things in this game effect the outcome. Such small details show up later and you wouldn't even know it unless you actually played it a second time. If you just played this once, then do it again. It's amazing. It sucks that you know what's coming, but the attention to details really show when you're not insanely sucked in to the story. A+ storytelling.
3rd playthrough:
So, you can google for some special keybindings for the Unreal engine and find how to apply them to games. so I did this and flew around all the different areas in this game. I recommend doing this as well. Just because you can get to areas that you weren't supposed to and it lets you see the developers approach to creating atmosphere. Yeah, there's nothing super special out there, you won't find any easter eggs, but it's just fun

Imagine for a moment, space travel with a complete disregard for safety. Instead of tirelessly assessing rockets to see if they will work, engineers just throw something together, plop some astronaughts in it, and send it on its way, often to a fiery end. Instead of checking fuel lines, or decouple joints, or even just the ability of a rocket to stay together, astronaughts get stranded in deep space when the command pod gets ejected instead of the empty fuel tanks, or the rockets break off from the rest of the spaceship and swoosh off into space. No calculations are made to ensure that the rocket has enough fuel to travel to it's destination, and mission after mission fails to even achieve orbit.
That is Kerbal Space program.
Trial and error is the name of the game (wait, isn't it called KSP?), and explosions are often the goal. If your first launch doesn't cause a Kerbonaught (Kerbals are the ingame species of space travellers) to die in horrific fashion, or leave most of the rocket on the launch pad because of an explosive malfunction, you are doing something wrong (or more accurately, right).
Essentially, if you enjoy space travel and designing contraptions (as sometimes you don't want a rocket, maybe a VTOL is more your style), this game is for you. If you enjoy setting your own goals and then setting them lower, this game is for you. If you are a rocket scientist, or if you are not a rocket scientist, this game is for you.
I suppose if you prefer to do things right, you can enjoy this game too. With the help of mods and/or a good understanding of space travel, you can easily develop rockets that work, but it is still very rewarding. Instead of trying to even crash into the Mun (in-game Moon) you can rather focus on building a space station around Jool (in-game Jupiter), or make the game harder by adding life support and communication networks.
Now, this game is not instant gratification, and it is not easy. If you prefer quick games, easy games, or games with specific goals, KSP may not be for you, but if you have even the slightest interest in space travel, buy this game, you will not regret it. KSP is a truly fantastic space program sim, simplified enough to make it fun, but still very focused on the true fundementals of rocketry: orbital mechanics, thrust to weight, specific impulse etc. (And trust me, if you get addicted, you'll figure out what those things all mean).
So throw caution to the wind and launch your skyscraper, or bring an asteroid crashing down to Kerbin (in-game Earth), or fly some kerbonaughts into the sun, it's your choice, and the sky isn't even close to the limit (or that would make for boring rocketry).

A refreshingly realistic take on spacefaring with a healthy dose of charm. Rather than fighting aliens or traveling faster than light, Kerbal Space Program takes you on a trek through the solar system with the kinds of rockets we've sent to the Moon. From reaching orbit to landing on other planets, every milestone you reach carries its own intense sense of accomplishment. The sandbox nature of the game lets you experiment with whatever rockets you'd like, while the career mode lets you take strides in the name of science! And, of course, once you've had your fun, there are a plethora of mods to keep you hooked for even longer.
Admittedly, the game is still rough around the edges (it is Early Access, after all!). Additionally, the learning curve for sending Kerbals to space is surprisingly steep. Once you've scaled that mountain, however, the sky's the limit.
Remember that thing about not traveling at the speed of light? There's a mod for that. Kerbal Space Program.

This is an incredible game, I've almost got 300 hours into it and I'm still looking forward to firing it up nearly every day.
There's a lot of reasons to buy this game:
* if you love space, this game will get you there, first hand, and let you have your hand at designing space crafts (and planes), flying them, and of course, crashing them in big glorious explosions
* you will learn a lot about space, physics, orbital mechanics, aerodynamics, etc... this really happens, I have two friends that are rocket scientists (one does ion drive research, the other designs micro-satellites, I work at a large university), and after playing this game for a few months, I could easily talk to them about their work, where they drop terms like ISP, TWR, retrograde, normals, etc, terms that I now fully understand
* the game is very approachable, you can play in "career mode" which walks you though the beginning steps of putting a rocket into space, to orbiting, to visiting the Mun and beyond. If you need more help, the YouTube scene is quite impressive, with people like Scott Manley producing really professional (and charming) video tutorial series. I am not a lover of simulation-type games, I play mostly FPS's and RPG's, but I found this game quite easy to pick and up get into.
* while approachable, this game is certainly not easy, for example, landing and returning from Eve (the Venus-like planet in the Kerbin system) is one of the hardest tasks in the game, and while most of the game is fairly non-stressful in its nature, landing spaceships is a tense experience, especially when Jeb's life is on the line! For those that find it difficult to master some of the more difficult tasks, there are impressive control mods like MechJeb2 where you essentially point at a spot on a planet and press the "Land There" button, MechJeb does the rest.
* the game has a unique charm to it, in the game you are progressing through the space race for the people of the Kerbin panet, you'll get to know and love the kerbalnauts that will fly your craft, especially Jebediah Kerman, pilot extraordinaire and fearless hero to the Kerbin people
* the community for this game, is active, organized, and quite friendly, mostly found on Reddit and the Squad forums, you can get any question answered, or read mission reports from someone's latest mission, or get news on upcoming updates for the game. The only time you see people getting belligerent on these forums is when some is misbehaving toward others
Squad is actively developing this game, each release (every new months) bringing a lot of new features and parts to build with, and just this week the update to KSP brings many new rocket parts built in collaboration with NASA plus a mission to save Kerbin from killer asteroids!
* the mod scene for this game is extremely impressive, from new real-life inspired rocket parts (so you can build your own Saturn V), to impressive new systems that enable for example planetary mining (so you can get more fuel on route to your target), to just plain fun mods like the nuclear pulse rocket, which explodes varied-sized nuclear bombs behind a large plate to produce thrust (scientists actually design this beast in the 50's)
* the endgame is rich and deep: once you've completed career mode, many KSP players switch to the realism mods, which give you the real solar system, truly deadly reentries, realistic communication constraints (that require building satellite networks), more realistic aerodynamics modeling (e.g., Ferram's amazing FAR mod), real life-support constraints, etc. that make for a significantly more challenging and rewarding experience; if that doesn't trip your trigger, the forums have organized challenges with leaderboards, to see who can, for example, get to the Mun with the least number of parts, or eject the most Kerbals out of the solar system, all great fun with the competitors meticulously documenting their missions
If these things sound interesting to you, get this game! It was the best $25 bucks I ever spent!

You have to be extra strict while reviewing "games" like Life is Strange™ since It has no actual gameplay. All you do is some basic exploration and make a few choices that supposedly matters. Since it starts off with a 0/10 in the gameplay department, the rest of the features are gonna have to really impress to make up for it.
They don't.
Spoilers ahead.
The time-travel mechanic, the main gimmick of this "game", is pants-on-head-♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. If Maxine walks by someone and turns back time a few seconds, it would look to the bystander as if she teleported because she herself doesn't move when she travels back in time. Nobody reacts to this. She's given these powers, f*ck knows why, and her first rewind causes the apocalypse, but its never explained why that one does it, or why on earth her using it for a billion other things doesn't.
Max is a poorly written character, barely more than a self-insert, never driven by anything other than other characters or what happens in her immediate vicinity at the time. She's also given TIME-TRAVEL and she barely experiments with it. One of the first things she uses it for is splashing paint on somebody she doesn't like. Talk about petty.
Only one choice in the entire game matters, all the way at the end, and its renders the entire game before that pointless.
The choice is either sacrificing Chloe, a massive c*nt no sane person could give two f*cks about, or sacrifice the entire town to a hurricane. Either of those happens regardless of what the player does throughout the "game". Some choice.
(How progressive of dontnod to make them lesbians for the hell(a) of it, It sure got the 'social justice warriors' on board)
The reason no sane person should give a sh*t about Chloe is that she's a useless, highschool drop-out stoner, a sadistic murderer (She kills a man she owes money to, and his dog too, why not..), she mooches of her parents money all the while being a disrespectful little tw*t who blames everyone else for her shortcomings.
You're supposed to care about this toxic person?
Speaking of being a sadistic murderer, in something of an alternate timeline, Maxine OD's a crippled nice version of Chloe for what I can only assume is for fun, because she rewinds and uncripples and unmurders her anyway.
Quotes from the horrible dialog:
"Wowser..." (over.. and over.. and over...)
"Why don't you go ♥♥♥♥ yourselfie"
"I just vaped some DANK OG BUD, so I can barely see you or these hotties next to me"
"You hella saved my life!"
"I can see why Chloe hangs here, she's a steampunk"
"You got hella cash"
"Let's talk bidness"
"Get off my crack, wh*re..." (admittedly, I chuckled at this, but knowing the writers, it was probably an oversight)
So to sum it all up,
Life is Strange™ is a pretentious story-driven game, where the story is awful with disgustingly bad dialogue and characters, where the only gameplay is walking around and making pointless choices. The music was okay.
Conclusion:
Want a bad movie? Go watch a bad movie.
Want a game with good storytelling?
Go play Silent Hill 1-3, the longest journey series, the witcher series, Metro 2033, Planescape: Torment, Metal Gear series, Beyond Good and Evil, and a metric tonne of other great games with actual gameplay as well as a story.
Anyone ever tell you that Life is Strange™ is a great game, they have no taste, and you can prompty disregard them and their hella bad, parroted opinions.

I randomly happened upon this game when Episode 1 first came out - I hadn't heard of it prior to that. Just looking at the screenshots and description, it looked like the kind of story-driven game I might be into. And I'm glad I bought it - Life is Strange is one of my favorite stories told through this medium, up there with the likes of Gone Home, the game that got me into this genre in the first place.
I graduated from high school about 5 years ago, so certainly a number of things aren't the same as when I was there -- but this game really captures the environment and feeling of high school as I remember it. From the beginning, I felt like I could relate to Max, the main character, and the experiences that she was having trying to fit in to a new school. Then the great twist, time travel, is thrown into the mix.
I won't spoil any of the story for you, as it is best experienced with no prior knowledge. Just know that you will be faced with many difficult decisions. If you are sensitive to themes of hard drugs, suicide, and/or bullying, be warned that this game features them extensively (but not in a way that glorifies them.)

Note: I've had this game for well over a half a year, I just now decided to make a review. :)
This being the first game I bought on Steam, I instantly fell in love. I saw various people do playthroughs on it, but I wanted to experience the game for myself before going ahead and spoiling the plot. I highly recommend doing the same.
Basic Story (No spoilers ^_^):
Life is Strange follows Max Caulfield, an 18-year-old high school Senior attending Blackwell Academy. The game opens up with eye-catching details; A specific girl being bullied, posters of a missing girl named Rachel, and the many characters who's faces will be shown in mulitple places overtime. The story becomes interesting quite fast. It doesn't leave you wondering, "Will there ever be something exciting soon?" Going any further may spoil some important events, so I'll refrain from doing so.
Each of the five episodes leaves you having more questions and desiring more answers. I won't lie, the amount of times I was moved by this game is way too damn many. Some of the decisions left me questioning myself and forced me to think "What if I didn't pick that?". The game Life is Strange forces you to use your head and heart in order to make a decision.
Don't even get me started on the soundtrack. I've played some games with excellent soundtracks, but Life is Strange has songs which stick with you. I cannot count the times I have found myself humming one of the many songs within this game. Life is Strange selected the greatest tracks which fit into every scene perfectly.
In all, I heavily recommend this game to anyone looking for a great storyline. Note that this game may not be everyone's cup of tea, but it does provide some sentimental feelings. If you're not fully sold on the entire game, I'd say just try out the first episode. (Though, I believe this game get really good around the third episode!)

It is so hard for me to put into words just how I feel about this game. When I received this game as a gift, I ended up playing an episode a night and becoming completely enraptured in the story, the characters, and just how many choices that I had. There's definitely a way to play through this game quickly and only make the major decisions that directly affect the story line, but there is so much more to explore and see. There are small things to discover and conversations to be had with other characters to further develop your relationships with them. Even though I was incredibly thorough on my first run through the game, I still managed to miss a conversation or two (especially with Brooke, oops). I also love how, at the end of each episode, you can compare the decisions you made throughout that episode with other players (although it sometimes made me feel guilty for choosing the less popular option haha).
But honestly, this game, in short, ripped me to pieces emotionally. I became so invested in Max and her best friend Chloe, and even in her "rival", Victoria, that when everything started to fall into place in the last episode, I was a sobbing mess. I can't wait to begin my second run through this game so I can experience everything again, and make some different choices. This game definitely has some incredible replay value. 10/10.
(On a side note, the soundtrack is AMAZING. I could just sit in the title screen, or in a Moment of Calm, or in Max's room with the stereo on and be completely content.)

A great game! It has only gotten better over time and the Career mode is still in developement but I love it! Could use some improvements and an actual currency system so I have a budget to work within but aside from that I love it, also you can make your own flags to stick on the Mun(yes that is Kerbin's moon), what more could you ask for!?
Anywho it's a space simulator game, not space simulator like freelancer or eve online but a make your own rocketship sim. Think of the spaceship creator in Spore...but actually good. You get tons of control, you can make accurate multi-stage rockets with center of gravity, weight, fuel, stability, etc. in mind and the best part is there's no boring tutorial you must go through in order to get the hang of the game, unlike other games where if you don't know what you're doing it's frustrating as hell, in KSP the failures you experience at the very beginning are quite amusing to watch, explosions, terrified kerbalnauts, accidentally releasing the parachute during liftoff, etc. are all very funny to see and you will learn from your mistakes in a way that won't make you mad.
All in all a great game, despite it being in early access for so long it is definitely worth buying. And what's more the newer stuff is consulted with NASA to be as accurate as possible without taking the fun out of the game :) see you on the Mun!

This being the first game I bought on Steam, I instantly fell in love. I saw various people do playthroughs on it, but I wanted to experience the game for myself before going ahead and spoiling the plot. I highly recommend doing the same.
Basic Story (No spoilers ^_^):
Life is Strange follows Max Caulfield, an 18-year-old high school Senior attending Blackwell Academy. The game opens up with eye-catching details; A specific girl being bullied, posters of a missing girl named Rachel, and the many characters who's faces will be shown in mulitple places overtime. The story becomes interesting quite fast. It doesn't leave you wondering, "Will there ever be something exciting soon?" Going any further may spoil some important events, so I'll refrain from doing so.
Each of the five episodes leaves you having more questions and desiring more answers. I won't lie, the amount of times I was moved by this game is way too damn many. Some of the decisions left me questioning myself and forced me to think "What if I didn't pick that?". The game Life is Strange forces you to use your head and heart in order to make a decision.
Don't even get me started on the soundtrack. I've played some games with excellent soundtracks, but Life is Strange has songs which stick with you. I cannot count the times I have found myself humming one of the many songs within this game. Life is Strange selected the greatest tracks which fit into every scene perfectly.
In all, I heavily recommend this game to anyone looking for a great storyline. Note that this game may not be everyone's cup of tea, but it does provide some sentimental feelings. If you're not fully sold on the entire game, I'd say just try out the first episode. (Though, I believe this game get really good around the third episode!)
This game is the best thing since sliced bread

It is so hard for me to put into words just how I feel about this game. When I received this game as a gift, I ended up playing an episode a night and becoming completely enraptured in the story, the characters, and just how many choices that I had. There's definitely a way to play through this game quickly and only make the major decisions that directly affect the story line, but there is so much more to explore and see. There are small things to discover and conversations to be had with other characters to further develop your relationships with them. Even though I was incredibly thorough on my first run through the game, I still managed to miss a conversation or two (especially with Brooke, oops). I also love how, at the end of each episode, you can compare the decisions you made throughout that episode with other players (although it sometimes made me feel guilty for choosing the less popular option haha).
But honestly, this game, in short, ripped me to pieces emotionally. I became so invested in Max and her best friend Chloe, and even in her "rival", Victoria, that when everything started to fall into place in the last episode, I was a sobbing mess. I can't wait to begin my second run through this game so I can experience everything again, and make some different choices. This game definitely has some incredible replay value. 10/10.
(On a side note, the soundtrack is AMAZING. I could just sit in the title screen, or in a Moment of Calm, or in Max's room with the stereo on and be completely content.)

An intense rollercoaster ride for the feels. The developers did a fantastic job with this game, creating characters that could be in your town, or the people you grew up with. The soundtrack fits the story perfectly, haunting and beautiful.

Actions actually have consequences, and you'll wonder, "What if I changed..." more than once. The choices you're given don't always have black & white answers, sometimes there is no "good" choice, and sometimes what you thought was right is the worst thing you can do.
Hopeful and funny, infuriating and terrifying. Life really is strange.
